sentences.zh: 列女二

translations.literal: Exemplary Women 2
translations.idiomatic: Exemplary Women 2

sentences.zh: 歐陽氏，九江人，彭澤王佳傅妻也。

translations.literal: The Ouyang clan—natives of Jiujiang, wife of Wang Jiafu of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ouyang was a native of Jiujiang and the wife of Wang Jiafu of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 事姑至孝。

translations.literal: She served her mother-in-law with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She served her mother-in-law with exemplary devotion.

sentences.zh: 夫亡，氏年方十八，撫遺腹子，紡績為生。

translations.literal: When her husband died, the lady was only eighteen; she reared the posthumous child and supported herself by spinning and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died, she was only eighteen. She raised their unborn child and earned a living by spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 父母迫之嫁，乃針刺其額，為誓死守節字，墨涅之，深入膚裏，里人稱為黑頭節婦。

translations.literal: Her parents pressed her to remarry; she then pricked her forehead with a needle, forming the characters vowing to guard her chastity unto death, blackened them with ink so they penetrated deep into the flesh, and the villagers called her the Black-Faced Chaste Widow.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents urged her to marry again, she pricked her forehead with a needle to tattoo a vow to remain chaste until death, rubbed ink into the wound until the characters were fixed deep in her skin, and her neighbors called her the Black-Faced Chaste Widow.

sentences.zh: 又徐氏，烏程人。

translations.literal: There was also the Xu clan, natives of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Xu of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 年十六，嫁潘順。

translations.literal: At sixteen she married Pan Shun.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen she married Pan Shun.

sentences.zh: 未期而夫病篤，顧徐曰：「母老，汝年少，奈何？」

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed her husband fell gravely ill and, turning to Xu, said: "My mother is old and you are young—what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed, her husband fell gravely ill. Looking at Xu, he said, "My mother is old and you are still young—what will become of you?"

sentences.zh: 徐泣下，即引刀斷左小指，以死誓。

translations.literal: Xu wept; she immediately drew a knife and severed her left little finger, swearing by death.
translations.idiomatic: Xu wept, then at once drew a knife and cut off her left little finger as a pledge unto death.

sentences.zh: 夫死，布衣長齋。

translations.literal: When her husband died, she wore plain cloth and kept a long fast.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband died, she wore plain hemp and observed a lifelong abstinence from meat and wine.

sentences.zh: 年七十八卒。

translations.literal: She died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺命取斷指入棺中。

translations.literal: She left instructions that the severed finger be placed in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In her final instructions she directed that the severed finger be placed in her coffin.

sentences.zh: 家人出其指，所染爪紅色尚存。

translations.literal: When the family took out the finger, the red stain from her nail polish was still there.
translations.idiomatic: When her family took out the finger, the red stain from her nail polish was still visible.

sentences.zh: 馮氏，宣城劉慶妻。

translations.literal: The Feng clan, wife of Liu Qing of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng was the wife of Liu Qing of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 年十九，夫亡，誓守節。

translations.literal: At nineteen her husband died, and she vowed to guard her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen her husband died, and she vowed to remain chaste.

sentences.zh: 其娣姒諷之曰：「守未易言，非咬斷鐵釘者不能。」

translations.literal: Her sisters-in-law mocked her, saying: "Chastity is not easily spoken of; none but one who can bite through an iron nail can do it."
translations.idiomatic: Her sisters-in-law mocked her, saying, "Chastity is easier said than done—only someone who can bite through an iron nail can keep it."

sentences.zh: 馮即投袂起，拔壁上釘嚙之，剨然有齒痕。

translations.literal: Feng at once flung up her sleeves, rose, pulled a nail from the wall, and bit it; with a crack there were tooth marks.
translations.idiomatic: Feng at once flung up her sleeves, rose, pulled a nail from the wall, and bit it through, leaving clear tooth marks.

sentences.zh: 復抉臂肉，釘著壁上曰：「脫有異志，此即狗彘肉不若。」

translations.literal: She then gouged flesh from her arm, nailed it to the wall, and said: "If I ever harbor a different intent, may this flesh be no better than that of dogs and swine."
translations.idiomatic: She then cut flesh from her arm, nailed it to the wall, and said, "If I ever waver in my resolve, may this flesh be no better than that of dogs and swine."

sentences.zh: 已而遺腹生子，曰大賢。

translations.literal: Later she bore a posthumous son named Daxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later she bore a posthumous son named Daxian.

sentences.zh: 長娶李氏，大賢又夭，姑婦相守至老。

translations.literal: When he grew up he married Lady Li; Daxian also died young, and mother-in-law and daughter-in-law kept each other company until old age.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he married Lady Li, but Daxian also died young, and mother-in-law and daughter-in-law remained together until the end of their lives.

sentences.zh: 卒，取視壁釘肉，尚韌不腐，齒痕如新。

translations.literal: When she died they took down the flesh nailed to the wall; it was still tough and uncorrupted, and the tooth marks were as fresh as new.
translations.idiomatic: When she died they took down the flesh nailed to the wall; it was still firm and uncorrupted, and the tooth marks looked as fresh as ever.

sentences.zh: 方氏，金華軍士袁堅妻。

translations.literal: The Fang clan, wife of Yuan Jian, a soldier of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fang was the wife of Yuan Jian, a soldier of Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 堅嗜酒敗家，卒殯城北濠上。

translations.literal: Jian was addicted to wine and ruined the family; when he died he was coffined on the north bank of the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was addicted to wine and ruined the family; when he died his coffin was placed on the north bank of the city moat.

sentences.zh: 方貧無所依，乃即殯處置棺，寢處其中，饑則出飲於濠。

translations.literal: Fang was poor and had nowhere to turn; she therefore set up a coffin at the place of encoffinment and slept within it, going out to drink from the moat when hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fang was destitute and had nowhere to turn. She set up a coffin at the burial place and slept inside it, going out to drink from the moat when she was hungry.

sentences.zh: 久之不復出，則死矣。

translations.literal: After a long time she did not come out again, and so she died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while she did not come out again, and so she died.

sentences.zh: 郡守劉郤為封土祭之。

translations.literal: The prefect Liu Qie had earth heaped up and offered sacrifice for her.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Liu Qie had a mound raised and offered sacrifice on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 又葉氏，蘭谿人。

translations.literal: There was also the Ye clan, a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Ye of Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 適神武中衛舍人許伸。

translations.literal: She was married to Xu Shen, a gentleman-attendant of the Divine Martial Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: She was married to Xu Shen, a gentleman-attendant of the Divine Martial Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 伸家素饒於財，以不檢，蕩且盡，攜妻投所親，卒於通州。

translations.literal: Shen's family had long been wealthy, but through lack of restraint he squandered it all; he took his wife to seek refuge with a kinsman and died at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu family had long been wealthy, but through his lack of restraint he squandered it all. He took his wife to seek refuge with a kinsman and died at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 氏守屍，晝夜跪哭。

translations.literal: The lady kept watch over the corpse, kneeling and weeping day and night.
translations.idiomatic: She kept vigil over his corpse, kneeling and weeping day and night.

sentences.zh: 或遺之食，或饋金，或勸以改嫁，俱卻不應。

translations.literal: Some brought her food, some offered gold, and some urged her to remarry; she refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: Some brought her food, some offered gold, and some urged her to remarry, but she refused them all.

sentences.zh: 水漿不入口者十四日，竟死屍傍，年二十餘，州人為買棺合葬。

translations.literal: For fourteen days she took neither water nor gruel, and in the end died beside the corpse; she was a little over twenty, and the people of the prefecture bought a coffin and buried them together.
translations.idiomatic: For fourteen days she took neither water nor food, and in the end died beside his corpse. She was a little over twenty, and the people of the prefecture bought a coffin and buried them together.

sentences.zh: 潘氏，海寧人。

translations.literal: The Pan clan, a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pan was a native of Haining.

sentences.zh: 年十六，歸許釗，生子淮。

translations.literal: At sixteen she married Xu Zhao and bore a son named Huai.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen she married Xu Zhao and bore a son named Huai.

sentences.zh: 甫期年，釗卒，既殮，潘自經。

translations.literal: Just after the first anniversary Zhao died; once he had been encoffined, Pan hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Just after their first anniversary Zhao died; once he had been encoffined, Pan hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 死已兩日矣，有老嫗過之曰：「是可活也。」

translations.literal: She had been dead two days when an old woman passed by and said: "She can still be revived."
translations.idiomatic: She had been dead two days when an old woman passed by and said, "She can still be revived."

sentences.zh: 投之藥，更蘇。

translations.literal: She administered medicine, and Pan revived.
translations.idiomatic: She gave her medicine, and Pan came back to life.

sentences.zh: 釗族兄欲不利於孤，嗾潘改適，潘毀容自矢。

translations.literal: Zhao's cousin by the clan wished harm upon the orphan and urged Pan to remarry; Pan disfigured her face and bound herself by vow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's cousin sought to harm the orphan and urged Pan to remarry, but she mutilated her face and bound herself by vow.

sentences.zh: 族兄者，夜率勢家仆數十人誣以債，椎門入。

translations.literal: That cousin, by night leading several dozen servants of powerful families, falsely charged them with debt and battered in the door.
translations.idiomatic: That cousin led several dozen henchmen's servants in the dead of night, falsely charged them with debt, and battered down the door.

sentences.zh: 潘負子，冒風雨，逾垣逸。

translations.literal: Pan carried her son on her back, braved wind and rain, scaled the wall, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pan took her son on her back, braved wind and rain, climbed over the wall, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 前距大河，追者迫，潘號慟投於河。

translations.literal: Ahead lay a great river; the pursuers pressed close. Pan wailed in grief and cast herself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: A great river lay ahead and the pursuers were closing in; Pan wailed in anguish and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 適有木浮至，憑以渡，達母家，遂止不歸。

translations.literal: Just then a piece of wood floated up; relying on it she crossed, reached her mother's home, and thereupon stayed without returning.
translations.idiomatic: A piece of driftwood happened to float by; she used it to cross, reached her mother's home, and stayed there without returning.

sentences.zh: 淮年十九，始歸。

translations.literal: When Huai was nineteen, she at last returned.
translations.idiomatic: She did not return until Huai was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 淮補諸生，娶婦生五子。

translations.literal: Huai enrolled as a licentiate, took a wife, and bore five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Huai enrolled as a licentiate, married, and had five sons.

sentences.zh: 潘年五十，宗人聚而祝，族兄者亦至。

translations.literal: When Pan was fifty, clansmen gathered to celebrate; that cousin also came.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan turned fifty, the clan gathered to celebrate; that cousin came as well.

sentences.zh: 潘曰：「氏所以得有今日，賴伯氏玉成。」

translations.literal: Pan said: "That this lady has come to have today is owed to Elder Clansman's having made it all come together."
translations.idiomatic: Pan said, "That I am where I am today is thanks to my elder clansman's having 'made it all come together."

sentences.zh: 目淮酌酒飲伯，卒爵，北向拜曰：「未亡人，三十年來瀕死者數矣，而顧強生，獨以淮故耳。

translations.literal: She looked at Huai to pour wine and had the elder drink; when the cup was empty she bowed facing north and said: "I, the not-yet-deceased woman, over thirty years have several times been on the brink of death, yet I forced myself to go on living — solely for Huai's sake.
translations.idiomatic: She signaled Huai to pour wine for the elder clansman; when he had drained his cup, she bowed toward the north and said, "As a widow, over the past thirty years I have been near death more than once, yet I forced myself to go on living — and only for Huai's sake.

sentences.zh: 今幸成立，且多子，復何憾。」

translations.literal: Now fortunately he is established, and moreover has many sons — what regret could remain?"
translations.idiomatic: Now he has fortunately come into his own, and has many sons besides — what more could I want?"

sentences.zh: 語畢入室。

translations.literal: When she had finished speaking she entered her room.
translations.idiomatic: When she had finished, she withdrew to her room.

sentences.zh: 頃之宴徹，諸宗人同淮入謝，則縊死室中矣。

translations.literal: Shortly the banquet ended; all the clansmen entered with Huai to thank her, and found her hanged dead in the room.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the feast was over; when the clansmen went in with Huai to thank her, they found she had hanged herself in her room.

sentences.zh: 楊氏，桐城吳仲淇妻。

translations.literal: The Yang clan, wife of Wu Zhongqi of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was the wife of Wu Zhongqi of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 仲淇卒，家貧，舅欲更嫁之。

translations.literal: Zhongqi died; the family was poor, and her father-in-law wished to have her remarry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongqi died the family was poor, and her father-in-law wanted to marry her off again.

sentences.zh: 楊曰：「即饑死，必與舅姑俱。」

translations.literal: Yang said: "Even if we starve to death, I must die together with my parents-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang said, "Even if we starve, I will die together with my parents-in-law."

sentences.zh: 舅不能奪。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law could not change her mind.
translations.idiomatic: Her father-in-law could not dissuade her.

sentences.zh: 數年，家益貧，舅謀於其父母，將以償債。

translations.literal: After several years the family grew still poorer; her father-in-law plotted with her parents to sell her to pay debts.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the family grew still poorer; her father-in-law conspired with her parents to sell her to pay off debts.

sentences.zh: 楊仰天呼曰：「以吾口累舅姑，不孝。

translations.literal: Yang cried to heaven: "To burden my parents-in-law with my mouth is unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang cried to heaven, "To burden my in-laws with my keep is unfilial.

sentences.zh: 無所助於貧，不仁。

translations.literal: To be of no help in poverty is unkind.
translations.idiomatic: To offer no relief to their poverty is unkind.

sentences.zh: 失節則不義。

translations.literal: To lose my chastity would be unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: To lose my chastity would be unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 吾有死而已。」

translations.literal: I have only death, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Death is all I have left."

sentences.zh: 因咽發而死。

translations.literal: She then died by swallowing hair.
translations.idiomatic: She killed herself by swallowing hair.

sentences.zh: 張烈婦，蕪湖諸生繆釜妻。

translations.literal: Chaste Wife Zhang, wife of the licentiate Miu Fu of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Wife Zhang was the wife of the licentiate Miu Fu of Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 年十八，歸釜。

translations.literal: At eighteen she married Fu.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she married Fu.

sentences.zh: 越四年，釜病，屬張善自托。

translations.literal: Four years later Fu fell ill and entrusted Zhang to take good care of herself.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, when Fu fell ill, he urged Zhang to look after herself.

sentences.zh: 張泣曰：「夫以吾有二心乎？

translations.literal: Zhang wept and said: "Does my husband think I have a divided heart?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang wept and said, "Does my husband think I am of two minds?

sentences.zh: 有子則守志奉主，妻道也。

translations.literal: If there is a son, then to keep one's resolve and serve the master is the wife's way.
translations.idiomatic: If there is a son, to keep faith and serve one's lord is a wife's duty.

sentences.zh: 無子則潔身殉夫，婦節也。」

translations.literal: If there is no son, then to preserve the body and die with the husband is a woman's chastity."
translations.idiomatic: If there is no son, to keep one's purity and follow one's husband in death is a woman's chastity."

sentences.zh: 乃沐浴更衣，闔戶自縊。

translations.literal: She then bathed, changed clothes, shut the door, and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She bathed, changed her clothes, shut the door, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 閱日，而釜乃卒。

translations.literal: The next day Fu finally died.
translations.idiomatic: A day later Fu died.

sentences.zh: 又蔡烈婦，松陽葉三妻。

translations.literal: Also Chaste Wife Cai, wife of Ye San of Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: Also Chaste Wife Cai, wife of Ye San of Songyang.

sentences.zh: 三負薪為業，蔡小心敬事。

translations.literal: San carried firewood for a living; Cai served him with careful reverence.
translations.idiomatic: San made his living carrying firewood; Cai served him attentively and respectfully.

sentences.zh: 三久病，織纴供藥餌。

translations.literal: San was long ill; she wove to supply medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When San was long ill, she wove to pay for his medicines.

sentences.zh: 病篤，執婦手訣曰：「及我生而嫁，無受三年苦。」

translations.literal: When the illness was grave he took his wife's hand in farewell and said: "Wait until I am dead to remarry; do not endure three years of hardship."
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, he clasped her hand in farewell and said, "Once I am dead, remarry — do not endure three years of hardship."

sentences.zh: 婦梳洗更衣，袖刀前曰：「我先嫁矣。」

translations.literal: The wife washed, changed clothes, hid a knife in her sleeve, and came forward saying: "I marry first."
translations.idiomatic: She washed, changed her clothes, hid a knife in her sleeve, and came forward saying, "I will marry first."

sentences.zh: 刎頸死。

translations.literal: She cut her throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: She cut her throat and died.

sentences.zh: 三驚嘆，尋死。

translations.literal: San exclaimed in amazement and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: San cried out in astonishment and soon died.

sentences.zh: 又鄭氏，安陸趙鈓妻。

translations.literal: Also Lady Zheng, wife of Zhao Ren of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lady Zheng was the wife of Zhao Ren of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 性剛烈，閨房中言動不涉非禮。

translations.literal: She was fierce in character; in the inner quarters her words and conduct never touched impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: She was fiercely upright; within the inner chambers her words and conduct never touched impropriety.

sentences.zh: 某寡婦更適人，饋以茶餅。

translations.literal: A certain widow remarried and sent tea and cakes as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: A certain widow remarried and sent tea and cakes as a gift.

sentences.zh: 鄭怒，命傾之。

translations.literal: Zheng was angered and ordered it poured out.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was enraged and ordered it thrown out.

sentences.zh: 夫戲曰：「若勿罵，幸夫不死耳。」

translations.literal: Her husband joked: "If you had not scolded, fortunately the husband would not have died."
translations.idiomatic: Her husband joked, "If you had not scolded her, I might not have died so soon."

sentences.zh: 鄭正色曰：「君勿憂，我豈為此者。」

translations.literal: Zheng said with a stern face: "My lord, do not worry — would I do such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said gravely, "My lord, do not worry — would I ever do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 後鈓疾將死，回視鄭，瞪目不瞑。

translations.literal: Later Ren fell gravely ill; as he was about to die he turned to look at Zheng, eyes staring, not closing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ren fell gravely ill and was near death, he turned to look at Zheng, his eyes wide open, unable to close them.

sentences.zh: 鄭曰：「君得毋疑我乎？」

translations.literal: Zheng said: "Does my lord perhaps doubt me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Does my lord perhaps doubt me?"

sentences.zh: 即自縊於床楣。

translations.literal: She immediately hanged herself from the bed frame.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately hanged herself from the bed frame.

sentences.zh: 鈓少蘇，回盼，出淚而絕。

translations.literal: Ren revived slightly, turned his gaze back, shed tears, and expired.
translations.idiomatic: Ren revived slightly, turned to look again, shed tears, and died.

sentences.zh: 王烈婦，上元人。

translations.literal: Chaste Wife Wang, a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Wife Wang was a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 夫嗜酒廢業，僦居破屋一間，以竹篷隔內外。

translations.literal: Her husband loved wine and neglected his livelihood; they rented one dilapidated room, with a bamboo mat partition separating inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband was a drunk who neglected his livelihood; they rented a single dilapidated room, divided inside and out by a bamboo screen.

sentences.zh: 婦日塞戶，坐門扉績麻自給。

translations.literal: Each day the wife blocked the door, sat at the doorway spinning hemp to support herself.
translations.idiomatic: Each day she barred the door and sat at the threshold spinning hemp to support herself.

sentences.zh: 夫與博徒李遊。

translations.literal: The husband associated with a gambler named Li.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband kept company with a gambler named Li.

sentences.zh: 李悅婦姿，謀亂之。

translations.literal: Li admired the wife's appearance and plotted to violate her.
translations.idiomatic: Li was taken with the wife's beauty and plotted to violate her.

sentences.zh: 夫被酒，以狂言餂婦，婦奔母家避之。

translations.literal: The husband, drunk, tried to win the wife with reckless talk; she fled to her mother's home to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband, drunk, tried to win her over with reckless talk; she fled to her mother's home to escape.

sentences.zh: 夫逼之歸，夜持酒脯與李俱至，引婦坐，婦駭走且罵。

translations.literal: The husband forced her to return; one night he brought wine and dried meat and came with Li, tried to make the wife sit; she fled in terror, cursing.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband forced her to return; one night he brought wine and dried meat and came with Li, tried to make her sit down, and she fled in terror, cursing them.

sentences.zh: 夫以威挾之，婦堅拒，大被搒笞。

translations.literal: The husband used threats to coerce her; she firmly refused and was severely beaten with rods.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband tried to coerce her by force; she firmly refused and was severely beaten.

sentences.zh: 婦度不免，夜攜幼女坐河干，慟哭投河死。

translations.literal: The wife judged she could not escape; at night she took her young daughter, sat by the riverbank, wept bitterly, and threw herself into the river to die.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, she took her young daughter one night, sat by the riverbank, wept bitterly, and threw herself into the river to die.

sentences.zh: 是夜，大風雨，屍不漂沒。

translations.literal: That night there was great wind and rain; the corpse did not drift away and sink.
translations.idiomatic: That night a great storm blew; her body did not drift away and sink.

sentences.zh: 及曙，女尚熟睡草間。

translations.literal: At dawn the daughter was still sleeping peacefully among the grass.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn her daughter was still sleeping peacefully in the grass.

sentences.zh: 又許烈婦，松江人許初女。

translations.literal: Also Chaste Wife Xu, daughter of Xu Chu of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Also Chaste Wife Xu, daughter of Xu Chu of Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 夫飲博不治生。

translations.literal: Her husband drank and gambled without attending to making a living.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband drank and gambled without earning a living.

sentences.zh: 諸博徒聚謀曰：「若婦少艾，曷不共我輩歡，日可得錢治酒。」

translations.literal: The gamblers gathered and plotted: "Your wife is young and fair — why not share her among us for pleasure? Each day you could get money for wine."
translations.idiomatic: The gamblers gathered and plotted, "Your wife is young and fair — why not let us all enjoy her? Each day you could get money for wine."

sentences.zh: 夫即以意喻婦，婦叱之，屢加箠撻不從。

translations.literal: The husband hinted this to his wife; she rebuked him and was repeatedly whipped with rods but would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband hinted as much to her; she rebuked him and was repeatedly beaten but would not yield.

sentences.zh: 一日，諸惡少以酒肴進。

translations.literal: One day the ruffians brought wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: One day the ruffians brought wine and food.

sentences.zh: 婦走避鄰嫗家，泣顧懷中女曰：「而父不才，吾安能顏自存，俟汝之成民也。」

translations.literal: The wife fled to a neighboring old woman's home, weeping as she looked back at the infant girl in her arms and said: "Your father is worthless — how can I preserve my face and go on living, waiting for you to become an adult?"
translations.idiomatic: She fled to a neighbor's home, weeping as she looked back at the infant girl in her arms and said, "Your father is worthless — how can I go on living with my honor intact, waiting for you to grow up?"

sentences.zh: 少間，聞闔戶聲。

translations.literal: After a little while she heard the sound of the door being shut.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later she heard the sound of a door closing.

sentences.zh: 嫗覘之，則拔刀刎頸仆地矣。

translations.literal: The old woman peeked and saw she had drawn a knife, cut her throat, and fallen to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman looked in and found she had drawn a knife, cut her throat, and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 父挈醫來視，取熱雞皮封之，復抓去。

translations.literal: Her father brought a doctor to see her; hot chicken skin was applied to seal the wound, but she tore it off again.
translations.idiomatic: Her father brought a doctor; hot chicken skin was applied to seal the wound, but she tore it off again.

sentences.zh: 明旦氣絕，年二十五。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day her breath ceased; she was twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: By the next morning she was dead; she was twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 吳氏，永豐人，名吉姑。

translations.literal: The Wu clan of Yongfeng, named Jigu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu of Yongfeng was named Jigu.

sentences.zh: 年十八，適寧集略。

translations.literal: At eighteen she married Ning Jilüe.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she married Ning Jilüe.

sentences.zh: 未一年，夫卒，六日不食。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed her husband died; she went six days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed her husband died, and she went six days without eating.

sentences.zh: 所親百方解譬，始食粥，朝暮一溢米。

translations.literal: Relatives tried every means to console her; she finally ate gruel, one dipper of rice morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives tried every means to comfort her; she finally ate gruel — one dipper of rice morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 服除，母憐其少，欲令改適。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, her mother pitied her youth and wished to have her remarry.
translations.idiomatic: When her mourning period ended, her mother pitied her youth and wanted her to remarry.

sentences.zh: 往視之，同寢食三年，竟不敢出一語。

translations.literal: She went to visit her; for three years they shared bed and meals, yet she never dared speak a word.
translations.idiomatic: She went to visit her; for three years they shared bed and meals, yet she never dared broach the subject.

sentences.zh: 歸謂諸婦曰：「此女鐵石心，不可動也。」

translations.literal: Returning home she told the other women: "This girl has a heart of iron and stone — she cannot be moved."
translations.idiomatic: Returning home she told the other women, "This girl has a heart of iron and stone — she cannot be moved."

sentences.zh: 慈谿沈氏六節婦。

translations.literal: Six Chaste Widows of the Shen clan of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Six Chaste Widows of the Shen clan of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 章氏，祚妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang, wife of Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, wife of Zuo.

sentences.zh: 周氏，希魯妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhou, wife of Xilu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou, wife of Xilu.

sentences.zh: 馮氏，信魁妻。

translations.literal: Lady Feng, wife of Xinkui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng, wife of Xinkui.

sentences.zh: 柴氏，惟瑞妻。

translations.literal: Lady Chai, wife of Weirui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chai, wife of Weirui.

sentences.zh: 孟氏，弘量妻。

translations.literal: Lady Meng, wife of Hongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Meng, wife of Hongliang.

sentences.zh: 孫氏，琳妻。

translations.literal: Lady Sun, wife of Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sun, wife of Lin.

sentences.zh: 所居名沈思橋，近海。

translations.literal: Their residence was called Shensi Bridge, near the sea.
translations.idiomatic: They lived at a place called Shensi Bridge, near the sea.

sentences.zh: 族眾二千人，多驍黠善鬥。

translations.literal: The clan numbered two thousand, mostly fierce, cunning, and skilled at fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The clan numbered two thousand, most of them fierce, cunning, and skilled fighters.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，倭賊入犯，屢殲其魁，奪還虜掠。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign, when Wokou raiders invaded, they repeatedly killed their leaders and recovered captives and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, when Wokou raiders invaded, the clan repeatedly killed their leaders and recovered captives and plunder.

sentences.zh: 賊深仇之。

translations.literal: The pirates deeply hated them.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates deeply hated them.

sentences.zh: 一日，賊大至，沈氏豪誓於眾曰：「無出婦女，無輦貨財，共以死守，違者誅。」

translations.literal: One day the pirates came in force; the Shen clan magnates swore to the assembly: "Do not send out women; do not cart away goods and wealth — all will defend to the death together; whoever disobeys will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: One day the pirates came in force; the Shen clan leaders swore to the assembly, "Do not send out the women; do not haul away goods and wealth — we will all defend this place to the death; whoever disobeys will be put to death."

sentences.zh: 章亦集族中婦女誓曰：「男子死鬥，婦人死義，無為賊辱。」

translations.literal: Zhang also gathered the clan's women and swore: "Let men die fighting; let women die for righteousness — do not be shamed by pirates."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang also gathered the clan's women and swore, "Let the men die fighting; let the women die for righteousness — do not let the pirates dishonor us."

sentences.zh: 眾竦息聽命。

translations.literal: All held their breath in awe and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: All stood in awed silence and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 賊圍合，群婦聚一樓以待。

translations.literal: The siege closed; the women gathered in one tower to wait.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege closed in, the women gathered in one tower to wait.

sentences.zh: 既而賊入，章先出投於河，周與馮從之。

translations.literal: When the pirates entered, Zhang went out first and threw herself into the river; Zhou and Feng followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates broke in, Lady Zhang went out first and threw herself into the river; Lady Zhou and Lady Feng followed.

sentences.zh: 紫方為夫礪刃，即以刃斫賊，旋自刃。

translations.literal: Lady Chai sharpened the blade for her husband, then used the blade to hack at the pirates, then turned it on herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chai sharpened a blade for her husband, then used it to hack at the pirates before turning it on herself.

sentences.zh: 孟與孫為賊所得，奪賊刃自刺死。

translations.literal: Meng and Sun were seized by the pirates; they snatched the pirates' blades and stabbed themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Meng and Lady Sun were seized by the pirates; they snatched the pirates' blades and stabbed themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 時宗婦死者三十餘人，而此六人尤烈。

translations.literal: At that time more than thirty clan women died, but these six were especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty clan women died that day, but these six were especially resolute.

sentences.zh: 黃氏，沙縣王珣妻。

translations.literal: Lady Huang, wife of Wang Xun of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huang was the wife of Wang Xun of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，倭亂，流劫其鄉。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign during the Wokou troubles, raiders swept through their district.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, in the Wokou troubles, raiders swept through their district.

sentences.zh: 鄉之比鄰，皆操舟為業。

translations.literal: Neighbors in the district all made their living by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Their neighbors in the district all made their living on the water.

sentences.zh: 賊至，眾婦登舟，匿艙中，黃兀坐其外。

translations.literal: When pirates came, all the women boarded boats and hid in the holds; Huang alone sat outside.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates came, the other women boarded boats and hid in the holds; Huang alone sat out in the open.

sentences.zh: 眾婦呼之曰：「不虞賊見乎？」

translations.literal: The women called to her: "Do you not fear the pirates will see you?"
translations.idiomatic: The other women called to her, "Are you not afraid the pirates will see you?"

sentences.zh: 黃曰：「篷窗安坐，恐賊至不得脫，我居外，便投水耳。」

translations.literal: Huang said: "Sitting safely inside the cabin — I fear when pirates come I will not be able to escape; I stay outside so I can throw myself into the water at once."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huang said, "If I sit safely inside the cabin, I fear that when the pirates come I will not be able to escape; I stay outside so I can throw myself into the water at once."

sentences.zh: 賊至，黃躍入水中死。

translations.literal: When the pirates came, Huang leaped into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates arrived, Lady Huang leaped into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 時同縣羅舉妻張氏，從夫避亂巖穴間。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Ju's wife Zhang of the same county followed her husband to escape the turmoil in rocky caves.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, Zhang, wife of Luo Ju of the same county, followed her husband into rocky caves to escape the chaos.

sentences.zh: 賊至，張與妾及妾子俱為所獲。

translations.literal: When the pirates came, Zhang together with the concubine and the concubine's son were all captured by them.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates arrived, Lady Zhang, the concubine, and the concubine's son were all seized.

sentences.zh: 賊見張美，欲犯之，不從。

translations.literal: The pirates saw Zhang was beautiful, wished to violate her, and she did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Lady Zhang was beautiful, the pirates tried to violate her, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 至中途，張解發自縊，賊斷之。

translations.literal: When they reached midway, Zhang loosened her hair and hanged herself; the pirates severed it.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway along the route, Lady Zhang let down her hair to hang herself; the pirates cut her down.

sentences.zh: 張又解行纏，賊又覺之，徒跣驅至營。

translations.literal: Zhang again undid her traveling wrappings; the pirates noticed again and drove her barefoot to the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang tried again, undoing her leg wrappings; the pirates caught her once more and drove her barefoot to their camp.

sentences.zh: 賊魁欲留之，張厲聲曰：「速賜一死。」

translations.literal: The pirate chief wished to keep her; Zhang said in a harsh voice: "Grant me death quickly."
translations.idiomatic: The pirate chief wanted to keep her; Lady Zhang cried out sharply, "Grant me a quick death."

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「不畏死，吾殺汝妾。」

translations.literal: The pirates said: "If you are not afraid of death, I will kill your concubine."
translations.idiomatic: The pirates said, "If you are not afraid to die, I will kill your concubine."

sentences.zh: 張引頸曰：「請代妾，留撫孩嬰。」

translations.literal: Zhang extended her neck and said: "Please take me instead of the concubine; leave her to tend the infant."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang thrust out her neck and said, "Take me instead of the concubine—let her remain to care for the child."

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「吾殺孩嬰。」

translations.literal: The pirates said: "I will kill the infant."
translations.idiomatic: The pirates said, "Then I will kill the infant."

sentences.zh: 張引頸曰：「請代孩嬰，存夫嗣。」

translations.literal: Zhang extended her neck and said: "Please take me instead of the infant; preserve my husband's male heir."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang thrust out her neck again and said, "Take me instead of the child—preserve my husband's line."

sentences.zh: 賊令牽出殺之。

translations.literal: The pirates ordered her led out and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates ordered her dragged out and executed.

sentences.zh: 張先行，了無懼色。

translations.literal: Zhang went first, with not the least trace of fear on her face.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang went first, showing not a trace of fear.

sentences.zh: 賊方猶豫，張罵不絕口，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The pirates were still hesitating; Zhang cursed without stopping and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: While the pirates still hesitated, Lady Zhang cursed them without cease—and was killed.

sentences.zh: 投屍於河，數日屍浮如生。

translations.literal: They cast the corpse into the river; after several days the corpse floated up as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: They threw her body into the river; several days later her corpse rose to the surface, looking as if she were still alive.

sentences.zh: 張氏，政和遊銓妻。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of You Quan of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang was the wife of You Quan of Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 倭寇將至，婦數語其女曰：「婦道惟節是尚，值變之窮，有溺與刃耳，汝謹識之。」

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates were about to arrive, the wife several times told her daughter: "Womanly conduct esteems chastity above all; when calamity leaves one at an impasse, there is only drowning and the blade — you must remember this."
translations.idiomatic: As the Wokou were about to arrive, she repeatedly told her daughter, "A woman's virtue lies in chastity alone; when disaster leaves no escape, there is only drowning or the blade—remember this well."

sentences.zh: 銓聞，以為不祥。

translations.literal: When Quan heard this, he regarded it as inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When You Quan heard this, he took it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 婦曰：「使婦與女能如此，祥孰大焉。」

translations.literal: The wife said: "If wife and daughter could act thus, what greater auspiciousness could there be?"
translations.idiomatic: His wife replied, "If my daughter and I could act thus, what greater blessing could there be?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊陷政和，張度不脫，連呼女曰：「省前誨乎？」

translations.literal: Before long, bandits captured Zhenghe; Zhang saw she could not escape and repeatedly called to her daughter: "Do you recall my earlier teaching?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the raiders sacked Zhenghe; seeing no escape, Lady Zhang called repeatedly to her daughter, "Do you remember what I taught you before?"

sentences.zh: 女頷之，即赴井。

translations.literal: The daughter nodded, then immediately went to the well.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter nodded and threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 張含笑隨之，並死。

translations.literal: Zhang smiled and followed; both died together.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang smiled and followed her; both died.

sentences.zh: 又葉氏，松溪江華妻，陳氏，葉弟惠勝妻，偕里人避倭長潭。

translations.literal: Also Ye, wife of Jiang Hua of Songxi; Chen, wife of Ye's younger brother Huishèng; together with fellow villagers they fled the Japanese pirates to Changtan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Ye, wife of Jiang Hua of Songxi, and Lady Chen, wife of Ye's younger brother Huishèng; together with their fellow villagers they fled the Wokou to Changtan.

sentences.zh: 值歲除，裏嫗覓刀為幼男發弗得，葉出諸懷中。

translations.literal: It being New Year's Eve, an old neighborhood woman looked for a knife to cut a young boy's hair but could not find one; Ye produced one from her bosom.
translations.idiomatic: It was New Year's Eve; an old woman in the lane needed a knife to cut a young boy's hair but could find none—Lady Ye produced one from inside her robe.

sentences.zh: 眾問故，曰：「以備急耳。」

translations.literal: The crowd asked the reason; she said: "To prepare for emergencies, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: When the others asked why, she said, "Only for emergencies."

sentences.zh: 及倭圍長潭，執二婦，共系一繩。

translations.literal: When the Japanese pirates surrounded Changtan, they seized the two women and bound them together on one rope.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wokou besieged Changtan, they seized the two women and bound them together with a single rope.

sentences.zh: 葉謂陳曰：「我二人被縶，縱生還，亦被惡名，死為愈。」

translations.literal: Ye said to Chen: "We two are bound; even if we return alive, we will still bear a foul name — death is better."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ye said to Lady Chen, "We two are captives; even if we survive and return home, we will be disgraced—it is better to die."

sentences.zh: 陳唯唯。

translations.literal: Chen assented repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen agreed.

sentences.zh: 葉探刀於懷，則已失，各抱幼女跳潭中死。

translations.literal: Ye searched for the knife in her bosom, but it was already gone; each embraced her young daughter and leaped into the pool to die.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ye searched inside her robe for the knife, but it was gone; each woman held her little daughter and leaped into the pool to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 同時林壽妻范氏，亦與眾婦匿山塢。

translations.literal: At the same time Lin Shou's wife Fan also hid with the other women in a mountain hollow.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, Lady Fan, wife of Lin Shou, was hiding with the other women in a mountain hollow.

sentences.zh: 倭搜得眾婦，偕至水南，範獨與抗。

translations.literal: The Japanese pirates searched out the women and took them together to Shuinan; Fan alone resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wokou found the women and marched them to Shuinan; Lady Fan alone resisted them.

sentences.zh: 或謂姑順之，家且來贖。

translations.literal: Some told her for the time being to submit, saying the family would soon come to redeem her.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged her to submit for now—the family would surely come to ransom her.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「身可贖，辱可贖哉！

translations.literal: She answered: "The body can be redeemed, but can dishonor be redeemed?
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "A body can be ransomed—but can dishonor?

sentences.zh: 我則寧死。」

translations.literal: As for me, I would rather die."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die."

sentences.zh: 賊聞言，殺其幼女恐之，不為勛。

translations.literal: When the pirates heard her words, they killed her young daughter to frighten her, but she was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates heard this, they killed her young daughter to terrify her, but she would not yield.

sentences.zh: 曰：「並及汝矣。」

translations.literal: They said: "You will be next."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "You will die as well."

sentences.zh: 厲聲曰：「固我願也！」

translations.literal: She said in a harsh voice: "That has always been my wish!"
translations.idiomatic: She cried out sharply, "That is exactly what I wish!"

sentences.zh: 賊殺之。

translations.literal: The pirates killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates killed her.

sentences.zh: 劉氏二女，興化人。

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Liu clan were people of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters of the Liu clan, from Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年與里中婦同為倭所掠，系路傍神祠中。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Jiajing they were together with village women captured by the Japanese pirates and bound in a roadside shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of the Jiajing reign, they were seized along with other village women by the Wokou and bound in a roadside shrine.

sentences.zh: 倭飲酣，遍視系中，先取其姊。

translations.literal: The Japanese pirates drank till drunk, looked over all who were bound, and first took the elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: The Wokou drank their fill, looked over everyone who was bound, and first took the elder sister.

sentences.zh: 姊厲聲曰：「我名家女也，肯汙賊乎？」

translations.literal: The elder sister said in a harsh voice: "I am a daughter of a distinguished family — would I submit to be defiled by bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: The elder sister cried out, "I am a daughter of a notable family—do you think I would let bandits defile me?"

sentences.zh: 倭笑慰之曰：「若從我，當詢父母歸汝。」

translations.literal: The Japanese pirate smiled and comforted her: "If you submit to me, I will inquire of your parents and return you to them."
translations.idiomatic: A Wokou smiled and tried to soothe her, "If you yield to me, I will ask your parents and send you home."

sentences.zh: 女曰：「父母未可知，此時尚論歸耶？」

translations.literal: The girl said: "Whether my parents still live is unknown — at such a time do you still speak of returning?"
translations.idiomatic: The girl replied, "Who knows whether my parents still live—and at a moment like this you speak of sending me home?"

sentences.zh: 倭尚撫背作款曲狀。

translations.literal: The Japanese pirate still stroked her back in a coaxing manner.
translations.idiomatic: The Wokou still stroked her back as if to coax her.

sentences.zh: 女怒，大罵。

translations.literal: The girl grew angry and cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The girl flew into a rage and cursed him loudly.

sentences.zh: 時黃昏，倭方縱火，女即赴火死。

translations.literal: It was dusk; the Japanese pirates had just set a fire; the girl immediately ran into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the Wokou set a fire; the girl ran straight into the flames and died.

sentences.zh: 已復侵其妹，妹又大罵。

translations.literal: Then they again violated the younger sister; the younger sister also cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned on the younger sister; she too cursed them loudly.

sentences.zh: 倭露刃脅之，不為動，曰：「欲殺，即殺。」

translations.literal: The Japanese pirate bared his blade to threaten her; she was not moved and said: "If you wish to kill, then kill."
translations.idiomatic: A Wokou drew his blade to threaten her; unmoved, she said, "If you want to kill me, then kill me."

sentences.zh: 倭欲強犯之，女紿曰：「吾固願從，俟姊骨燼乃可，否則不忍也。」

translations.literal: The Japanese pirate wished to force her; the girl deceived him and said: "I indeed wish to submit — wait until my sister's bones are ash; otherwise I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: He tried to force himself on her; the girl feigned compliance and said, "I am willing—but only after my sister's bones are burned to ash; until then I cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 倭喜負薪益火，火熾，女又赴火死。

translations.literal: The Japanese pirate gladly shouldered firewood to increase the fire; when the fire blazed, the girl again ran into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Wokou piled on wood until the flames leaped high; the girl ran into the fire again and died.

sentences.zh: 時同死者四十七人，二女為最。

translations.literal: At the time forty-seven died together; the two daughters were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-seven died together that day; of them all, the two sisters were the most resolute.

sentences.zh: 孫烈女，五河人。

translations.literal: Sun the chaste maiden, a person of Wuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Sun the chaste maiden was from Wuhe.

sentences.zh: 性貞靜，不茍嬉笑。

translations.literal: Her nature was chaste and quiet; she did not laugh or jest casually.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste and reserved by nature, she never laughed or jested lightly.

sentences.zh: 母朱卒，繼母李攜前夫子鄭州兒來。

translations.literal: When her mother Zhu died, stepmother Li brought her former husband's son Zheng Zhou'er.
translations.idiomatic: After her mother Zhu died, her stepmother Li arrived with Zhou, her son from a previous marriage.

sentences.zh: 州兒恃母欲私女，嘗以手挑之，忿批其頰。

translations.literal: Zhou'er relied on his mother and wished to have private relations with the girl; once he teased her with his hand and she angrily slapped his cheek.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou'er, emboldened by his mother's presence, tried to seduce her; once he touched her with his hand, and she slapped his face in fury.

sentences.zh: 一日，女方治面，州兒從後摟之。

translations.literal: One day, as the girl was attending to her face, Zhou'er embraced her from behind.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while she was at her toilet, Zhou'er grabbed her from behind.

sentences.zh: 女揪發覓刃，州兒嚙其臂得脫。

translations.literal: The girl grabbed her hair and searched for a blade; Zhou'er bit her arm and got free.
translations.idiomatic: She seized her hair and searched for a knife; Zhou'er bit her arm and broke free.

sentences.zh: 女奔訴於姊，觸地慟哭曰：「母不幸，父又他出，賊子敢辱我，必刃之而後死。」

translations.literal: The girl ran to tell her elder sister, fell to the ground weeping and said: "Mother has met with misfortune, father is also away on business — this villain dares dishonor me; I must blade him before I die."
translations.idiomatic: She ran to her elder sister, threw herself to the ground, and wept, "Mother is gone, and Father is away—this villain dares dishonor me; I will cut him down before I die."

sentences.zh: 姊曲撫慰。

translations.literal: The elder sister gently comforted and reassured her.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister gently comforted her.

sentences.zh: 乃以臂痕示李，使戒戢之。

translations.literal: She then showed the arm wound to Li and had her warn and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: She showed the bite mark on her arm to Li and asked her to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 州兒不悛，紿李曰：「兒采薪，臂力不勝，置遺束於路。」

translations.literal: Zhou'er did not repent; he deceived Li saying: "Your son went to gather firewood; my arm strength could not manage it; I left a dropped bundle on the road."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou'er would not mend his ways; he tricked Li, saying, "I was gathering firewood but could not carry it all—I left a bundle on the road."

sentences.zh: 李往取之，歸則戶扃甚嚴。

translations.literal: Li went to fetch it; when she returned the door was bolted very tightly.
translations.idiomatic: Li went to fetch it; when she returned, the door was bolted shut.

sentences.zh: 從母舒氏亦趨至，曰：「初聞如小犢悲鳴，繼又響震如雷，必有異。」

translations.literal: Her mother's younger sister Shu also hurried over and said: "At first I heard something like a calf's mournful cry, then a sound shaking like thunder — there must be something wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Her aunt Shu hurried over as well and said, "At first I heard something like a calf lowing in distress, then a crash like thunder—something is wrong."

sentences.zh: 並力啟之，州兒死閾下，項幾斷，女亦倚壁死。

translations.literal: Together they forced it open; Zhou'er was dead beneath the threshold, his neck nearly severed; the girl also leaned against the wall dead.
translations.idiomatic: Together they forced the door open: Zhou'er lay dead below the threshold, his neck nearly severed; the girl sat dead against the wall.

sentences.zh: 蓋州兒誑母出，調女。

translations.literal: It turned out Zhou'er had deceived his mother into going out to seduce the girl.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou'er had tricked his mother into going out so he could molest the girl.

sentences.zh: 女陽諾而使之閉門，既躡其後殺之也。

translations.literal: The girl feigned consent and had him close the door, then stole up behind him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: She had pretended to yield and told him to bolt the door, then killed him from behind.

sentences.zh: 又蔡烈女，上元人。

translations.literal: Also Cai the chaste maiden, a person of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cai the chaste maiden, from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，與祖母居。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, she lived with her grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she lived alone with her grandmother.

sentences.zh: 一日，祖母出，有逐仆為僧者來乞食，挑之，不從。

translations.literal: One day when grandmother went out, a monk who had been a chased-away servant came to beg food, molested her, and she did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: One day her grandmother went out; a disgraced servant who had become a monk came begging for food, tried to molest her, and she refused.

sentences.zh: 挾以刃，女徒手搏之，受傷十餘處，罵不絕，宛轉死竈下。

translations.literal: He threatened her with a blade; the girl fought him bare-handed, received wounds in more than ten places, cursed without stopping, and writhed to death beneath the stove.
translations.idiomatic: He threatened her with a knife; she fought him bare-handed, suffering more than ten wounds, cursing him without cease until she died writhing beneath the stove.

sentences.zh: 賊遁去，官行驗，忽來首伏。

translations.literal: The villain fled; when officials came to inspect the scene, he suddenly came forward to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The assailant fled; when officials arrived to investigate, he suddenly appeared to confess.

sentences.zh: 官怪問故。

translations.literal: The officials wondered and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The officials were astonished and asked why.

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「女拘我至此。」

translations.literal: The villain said: "The girl bound me to come here."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "The girl compelled me to come here."

sentences.zh: 遂抵罪。

translations.literal: He was therefore punished according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted and punished.

sentences.zh: 陳諫妻李氏，番禺人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Chen Jian, from Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li, wife of Chen Jian, was from Panyu.

sentences.zh: 諫，嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jian was a jinshi of the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jian passed the metropolitan examination in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 為太平推官，兩月卒，其弟扶櫬歸。

translations.literal: He served as investigating censor of Taiping, died after two months; his younger brother escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Taiping and died within two months; his younger brother escorted the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 李曰：「吾少嫠也，豈可與叔萬里同歸哉！」

translations.literal: Li said: "I have been a widow since youth — how can I travel ten thousand li home with my husband's younger brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li said, "I have been a widow since I was young—how could I travel a thousand miles home with my husband's younger brother!"

sentences.zh: 遂不食死。

translations.literal: She therefore refused food and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then refused food until she died.

sentences.zh: 胡氏，會稽人。

translations.literal: Hu, a person of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hu was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 字同里沈袠。

translations.literal: She was betrothed to Shen Zhi of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to Shen Zhi, a man of the same district.

sentences.zh: 將嫁，而袠遘父煉難，二兄袞、褒杖死塞上，袠與兄襄並逮系宣府獄。

translations.literal: About to marry, Zhi encountered his father's ordeal by interrogation under torture; two elder brothers Gun and Bao were beaten to death on the frontier; Zhi and elder brother Xiang were both arrested and imprisoned in Xuanfu jail.
translations.idiomatic: Just before the wedding, Shen Zhi's father was caught in a political purge; two of his elder brothers, Gun and Bao, were beaten to death on the frontier; Zhi and another brother, Xiang, were arrested and imprisoned at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 總督楊順逢嚴嵩意，必欲置二子死，搒掠數百，令夜分具二子病狀。

translations.literal: Governor-general Yang Shun, acting in accord with Yan Song's intent, was determined to put the two sons to death; after several hundred beatings, he ordered that by midnight reports of the two sons' illness be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general Yang Shun, eager to please Yan Song, was resolved to kill the two brothers; after hundreds of blows he ordered that, by midnight, medical reports documenting their fatal illness be submitted.

sentences.zh: 會順為給事中吳時來所劾，就檻車去，襄等乃得釋。

translations.literal: Just then Yang was impeached by supervising secretary Wu Shilai and departed in a caged cart; Xiang and the others were then released.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang was impeached by the supervising secretary Wu Shilai and led away in a prisoner cart, Xiang and the others were finally released.

sentences.zh: 自是病嘔血，扶父喪歸，比服闋始婚，胡年已二十七。

translations.literal: From then on he was ill vomiting blood; he escorted his father's coffin home, and only when mourning ended did he marry; Hu was already twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi thereafter suffered from coughing blood; he escorted his father's coffin home and did not marry until mourning was complete—by then Hu was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 逾六月，袠卒，胡哀哭不絕聲，盡出奩具治喪事。

translations.literal: After six months Zhi died; Hu wept without cease, emptied all her dowry to manage the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Six months later Zhi died; Lady Hu wailed without cease and spent her entire dowry on the funeral.

sentences.zh: 有他諷者，斷發剺面絕之。

translations.literal: When someone importuned her with other matchmaking proposals, she cut her hair and scarred her face to break off relations.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone urged her to remarry, she cut her hair and disfigured her face to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 終日一室中，即同產非時不見。

translations.literal: All day within one room; even full siblings she would not see except at proper times.
translations.idiomatic: She remained in one room all day and would not even receive her own siblings except at appointed times.

sentences.zh: 晚染疾，家人將迎醫，告其父曰：「寡婦之手豈可令他人視。」

translations.literal: Late in life she fell ill; when the family was about to summon a doctor, she told her father-in-law: "Can a widow's hand be looked upon by others?"
translations.idiomatic: In her later years she fell ill; when her family tried to send for a doctor, she told her father-in-law, "Can a widow's hands be seen by strangers?"

sentences.zh: 不藥而卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: She took no medicine and died, at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: She refused medicine and died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 以襄子嗣。

translations.literal: Xiang's son was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: She adopted Xiang's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 戴氏，莆田人，名清。

translations.literal: Dai, from Putian, named Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dai, from Putian, was called Qing.

sentences.zh: 歸蔡本澄，年甫十四。

translations.literal: She married Cai Bencheng at just fourteen years of age.
translations.idiomatic: She married Cai Bencheng when she was only fourteen.

sentences.zh: 居二年，本澄以世籍戍遼東，買妾代婦行。

translations.literal: After two years Bencheng due to hereditary military registration was posted to guard Liaodong; he bought a concubine to go in the wife's place.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, Bencheng was conscripted for frontier service in Liaodong on account of hereditary registration; he bought a concubine to take his wife's place on the march.

sentences.zh: 戴父與約曰：「遼左天末，五年不歸，吾女當改嫁矣。」

translations.literal: Qing's father made an agreement saying: "Liaodong is at heaven's edge; if he does not return in five years, my daughter should remarry."
translations.idiomatic: Qing's father struck a bargain with him: "Liaodong is at the ends of the earth; if you are not home within five years, my daughter may remarry."

sentences.zh: 至期，父語清如約。

translations.literal: When the term arrived, her father told Qing according to the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: When the five years were up, her father told Qing of the agreement.

sentences.zh: 泣不從，獨居十有五年。

translations.literal: She wept and refused; she lived alone for fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: She wept and refused; she lived alone for fifteen years more.

sentences.zh: 本澄歸，生一子，未晬，父子相繼亡。

translations.literal: Bencheng returned and a son was born; before the child reached one year, father and son died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Bencheng returned, and she bore a son; before the baby was a year old, husband and child died in succession.

sentences.zh: 清哀毀幾絕。

translations.literal: Qing's mourning grief nearly killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Qing grieved so deeply she nearly died of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 父潛受吳氏聘，清聞之曰：「人呼女蔡本澄婦耳，何又云吳耶？」

translations.literal: Her father secretly accepted a betrothal from the Wu clan; when Qing heard of it she said: "People call me the wife of Cai Bencheng—why should they now speak of the Wus?"
translations.idiomatic: Her father secretly accepted a betrothal from the Wu clan. When Qing heard of it, she said, "People call me the wife of Cai Bencheng—why should anyone now speak of the Wus?"

sentences.zh: 即往父家，使絕婚。

translations.literal: She went at once to her father's house and made him break off the engagement.
translations.idiomatic: She went at once to her father's house and made him break off the engagement.

sentences.zh: 吳訟之官，令守節，表曰寡婦清之門。

translations.literal: The Wus sued at the yamen; the magistrate ordered her to maintain chastity and erected an archway inscribed "The Gate of Widow Qing."
translations.idiomatic: The Wus brought suit at the yamen; the magistrate ordered her to maintain chastity and erected an archway inscribed "The Gate of Widow Qing."

sentences.zh: 時莆又有歐茂仁妻胡氏，守節嚴苦，內外重之。

translations.literal: At that time in Pu there was also Hu, wife of Ou Maoren, whose chaste widowhood was stern and arduous; inside and outside the household she was respected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in Pu there was also Hu, wife of Ou Maoren, whose chaste widowhood was stern and arduous, and she was respected both within her household and beyond it.

sentences.zh: 郡有獄久不斷，人曰：「太守可問胡寡婦。」

translations.literal: In the commandery was a case long unresolved; people said: "The governor should consult Widow Hu."
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery was a case long unresolved; people said, "The governor should consult Widow Hu."

sentences.zh: 守乃過婦問之，一言而決。

translations.literal: The governor then visited the woman to ask her, and with one word the case was decided.
translations.idiomatic: The governor then visited the woman to ask her, and with a single word the case was decided.

sentences.zh: 胡氏，鄞許元忱妻。

translations.literal: Hu was wife of Xu Yuanchen of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hu was wife of Xu Yuanchen of Yin.

sentences.zh: 元忱為徐祝師養子，習巫祝事。

translations.literal: Yuanchen was an adopted son of the Xu shaman-priest family and trained in shamanic rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen was an adopted son of the Xu shaman-priest family and had been trained in shamanic rites.

sentences.zh: 胡鄙之，勸夫改業，且勸歸許宗。

translations.literal: Hu despised this and urged her husband to change his occupation, and also urged him to rejoin the Xu lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Hu despised this life and urged her husband to change his occupation and to rejoin the Xu lineage.

sentences.zh: 未果，而元忱疫死。

translations.literal: Before this was achieved, Yuanchen died of pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Before this could be achieved, Yuanchen died of pestilence.

sentences.zh: 氏殯之許氏廬，苫臥柩傍，夜擁一刀臥。

translations.literal: She laid out his body at a Xu clan hall, slept on straw beside the coffin, and at night slept clutching a knife.
translations.idiomatic: She laid out his body in a Xu clan hall, slept on straw beside the coffin, and at night slept clutching a knife.

sentences.zh: 裏某求氏為偶，氏毀面截鬢髮，斷左手三指，流血淋漓，某驚遁。

translations.literal: A certain man of Li sought her for marriage; she defaced her face, cut off her side locks and hair, and severed three fingers of her left hand; blood poured freely, and the man fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: A certain man of Li sought her for marriage; she disfigured her face, cut off her side locks and hair, and severed three fingers of her left hand; blood poured freely, and the man fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 族婦尊行抱持之，大慟，因立應後者，令子之。

translations.literal: An elder woman of the clan held her in her arms and wailed greatly; she then established a male heir and adopted him as son.
translations.idiomatic: An elder woman of the clan held her in her arms and wailed greatly; she then established a male heir and adopted him as her son.

sentences.zh: 氏服喪三年，不浣不櫛。

translations.literal: She observed mourning for three years without washing or combing her hair.
translations.idiomatic: She observed mourning for three years without washing or combing her hair.

sentences.zh: 畢葬，乃為子娶婦。

translations.literal: When burial was complete, she then found a wife for her son.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was complete, she found a wife for her son.

sentences.zh: 夫有弟少流移於外，復為返之，許氏賴以復起。

translations.literal: Her husband had a younger brother who as a youth had drifted away; she brought him back, and the Xu clan thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband had a younger brother who as a youth had drifted away; she brought him back, and the Xu clan thereby revived.

sentences.zh: 李氏，郃陽安尚起妻。

translations.literal: Li was wife of An Shangqi of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was wife of An Shangqi of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 尚起商河南，病亡。

translations.literal: Shangqi traded in Henan and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shangqi traded in Henan and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 氏聞訃，盡變產完夫債，且置棺以待夫櫬歸，跪告族黨曰：「煩舉二棺入地。」

translations.literal: When she heard the death notice, she sold all her property to settle her husband's debts, prepared a coffin to await his return, and kneeling told the clan: "I trouble you to lower two coffins into the earth."
translations.idiomatic: When she heard the death notice, she sold all her property to settle her husband's debts, prepared a coffin to await his return, and kneeling told the clan, "I ask you to lower two coffins into the earth."

sentences.zh: 閉戶將自縊，鄰婦欲生之，排闥曰：「爾尚有所逋，何遽死？」

translations.literal: She closed the door intending to hang herself; a neighbor woman wishing to save her broke in and said: "You still have outstanding debts—why hurry to die?"
translations.idiomatic: She closed the door intending to hang herself; a neighbor woman wishing to save her broke in and said, "You still have outstanding debts—why hurry to die?"

sentences.zh: 氏啟門應曰：「然吾資已盡，奈何？

translations.literal: She opened the door and replied: "But my means are exhausted—what can I do?
translations.idiomatic: She opened the door and answered, "But I have exhausted my means—what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 請復待一日。」

translations.literal: Please wait one more day."
translations.idiomatic: Please wait one more day."

sentences.zh: 乃紉履一雙往畀之，曰：「得此足償矣。」

translations.literal: She then sewed a pair of shoes and brought them to pay the debt, saying: "With this I am fully repaid."
translations.idiomatic: She then sewed a pair of shoes and brought them to pay the debt, saying, "With this the debt is fully repaid."

sentences.zh: 歸家，遂縊死。

translations.literal: She returned home and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She returned home and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 吳節婦，無為周凝貞妻。

translations.literal: Chaste Widow Wu was wife of Zhou Ningzhen of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Widow Wu was wife of Zhou Ningzhen of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 凝貞卒，婦年二十四，毀容誓死，不更適，傭女工以奉孀姑。

translations.literal: When Ningzhen died, the wife was twenty-four; she disfigured herself, swore to die, refused remarriage, and hired out as a seamstress to support her widowed mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzhen died, the wife was twenty-four; she disfigured herself, swore to die rather than live, refused remarriage, and hired out as a seamstress to support her widowed mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑老臥病，齒毀弗能食。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law was old, bedridden, and her teeth ruined so she could not eat.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law was old and bedridden; her teeth were ruined and she could not eat.

sentences.zh: 婦絕其兒乳以乳姑，冬月臥擁姑背以暖之，宛轉床席者三年。

translations.literal: The wife stopped nursing her own child to nurse her mother-in-law; in winter she slept embracing her mother-in-law's back to warm her, turning this way and that upon the bed for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The wife weaned her own child so she could nurse her mother-in-law; in winter she slept embracing her mother-in-law's back to warm her, turning this way and that upon the bed for three years.

sentences.zh: 姑卒，哀毀骨立，年七十五終。

translations.literal: When the mother-in-law died, she grieved until her bones stood bare; she died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: When the mother-in-law died, she grieved until her bones stood bare; she died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 又楊氏，清苑劉壽昌妻。

translations.literal: Also Yang, wife of Liu Shouchang of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lady Yang, wife of Liu Shouchang of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 年十九，夫卒，誓死殉。

translations.literal: At nineteen her husband died; she swore to die in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen her husband died; she swore to die with him.

sentences.zh: 念姑病無依，乃不死。

translations.literal: Seeing her mother-in-law ill and with no one to rely on, she did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing her mother-in-law ill and with no one to rely on, she did not die.

sentences.zh: 母家來迎，以姑老不忍去側，竟不歸寧。

translations.literal: Her natal family came to fetch her, but because her mother-in-law was old she could not bear to leave her side and never returned for visits home.
translations.idiomatic: Her natal family came to fetch her, but because her mother-in-law was old she could not bear to leave her side and never returned home for visits.

sentences.zh: 閱三十年，姑卒，葬畢，哀號夫墓曰：「妾今得相從地下矣。」

translations.literal: After thirty years her mother-in-law died; when burial was done, she wailed at her husband's grave: "Your handmaid may now follow you underground."
translations.idiomatic: After thirty years her mother-in-law died; when the burial was complete, she wailed at her husband's grave, "Your handmaid may now follow you underground."

sentences.zh: 遂絕粒。

translations.literal: She then stopped eating.
translations.idiomatic: She then stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 家人問遺言。

translations.literal: The family asked her final wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The family asked her final wishes.

sentences.zh: 曰：「姑服在身，殮以布素。」

translations.literal: She said: "Mourning garb for my mother-in-law is still on me—bury me in plain cloth."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Mourning garb for my mother-in-law is still on me—bury me in plain cloth."

sentences.zh: 遂瞑。

translations.literal: Then she closed her eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Then she closed her eyes.

sentences.zh: 徐亞長，東莞徐添男女。

translations.literal: Xu Yachang was daughter of Xu Tiannan of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yachang was daughter of Xu Tiannan of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 添男為徐姓仆，生亞長四歲而死。

translations.literal: Tiannan was a servant of the Xu surname family; he bore Yachang and died when she was four.
translations.idiomatic: Tiannan was a servant of the Xu clan; he fathered Yachang and died when she was four.

sentences.zh: 母以亞長還其主，去而別適。

translations.literal: Her mother returned Yachang to the master and departed to marry elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother returned Yachang to the master and departed to marry elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 比長，貞靜寡言笑，居群婢中，凜然有難犯之色。

translations.literal: When she grew up, she was chaste and quiet, rarely speaking or smiling; among the maidservants she had an austere bearing difficult to violate.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up, she was chaste and quiet, rarely speaking or smiling; among the maidservants she had an austere bearing that none dared violate.

sentences.zh: 家童進旺欲私之，不可。

translations.literal: A houseboy named Jinwang sought intimacy with her but could not.
translations.idiomatic: A houseboy named Jinwang sought intimacy with her but could not.

sentences.zh: 亞長奉主命草豆田中，進旺跡而迫之，力拒獲免，因哭曰：「聞郎君讀書，有寡婦手為人所引，斧斷其手，況我尚女也，何以生為！」

translations.literal: Yachang was ordered by her master to weed the bean field; Jinwang tracked her and pressed close; she resisted with force and escaped, then wept: "I hear the young master reads books—when a widow's hand was led astray by a man, an axe severed it; how much more I, still an unmarried girl—what reason have I to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Yachang was ordered by her master to weed the bean field; Jinwang tracked her and pressed close; she resisted with force and escaped, then wept, "I hear the young master reads books—when a widow's hand was led astray by a man, an axe severed it; and I am still an unmarried girl—what reason have I to live!"

sentences.zh: 遂投江死。

translations.literal: She then threw herself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then threw herself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 蔣烈婦，丹陽姜士進妻。

translations.literal: Chaste Wife Jiang was wife of Jiang Shijin of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Wife Jiang was wife of Jiang Shijin of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，喜讀書。

translations.literal: From youth she was quick-witted and loved reading books.
translations.idiomatic: From youth she was quick-witted and loved reading books.

sentences.zh: 弟文止方就外傅。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Wenzhi had just begun studying with an outside tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Wenzhi had just begun studying with an outside tutor.

sentences.zh: 夜歸，輒以餅餌啖之，令誦日所授書，悉能記憶，久之遂能文。

translations.literal: When he came home at night, she would feed him cakes and snacks and make him recite the day's lessons; he could remember them all, and in time he came to write essays.
translations.idiomatic: When he came home at night, she would feed him cakes and snacks and make him recite the day's lessons; he could remember them all, and in time he learned to write essays.

sentences.zh: 歸士進數年，士進病瘵死。

translations.literal: After several years of marriage to Shijin, Shijin died of consumption.
translations.idiomatic: After several years of marriage to Shijin, Shijin died of consumption.

sentences.zh: 婦屑金和酒飲之，並飲鹽鹵。

translations.literal: The wife mixed gold filings with wine and drank it, also drinking brine.
translations.idiomatic: The wife mixed gold filings with wine and drank it, and also drank brine.

sentences.zh: 其父數偵知，奔救免。

translations.literal: Her father repeatedly spied this out and rushed to save her.
translations.idiomatic: Her father repeatedly discovered this and rushed to save her.

sentences.zh: 不食者十二日，父啟其齒飲之藥，復不死。

translations.literal: For twelve days she ate nothing; her father forced open her teeth and poured in medicine, and again she did not die.
translations.idiomatic: For twelve days she ate nothing; her father forced open her teeth and poured in medicine, and again she did not die.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書寶，士進從父也，知婦嗜讀書，多置古圖史於其寢所，令續劉向《列女傳》。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Bao—Shijin's paternal uncle—knowing the wife loved reading, placed many ancient illustrated histories in her bedroom and had her continue Liu Xiang's "Biographies of Exemplary Women."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Jiang Bao—Shijin's paternal uncle—knowing the wife loved reading, placed many ancient illustrated histories in her bedroom and had her continue Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 婦許諾，家人備之益謹。

translations.literal: The wife agreed; the family kept watch all the more strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The wife agreed; the family kept watch all the more strictly.

sentences.zh: 一日，婦命於繐帳前掘坎埋大缸貯水，笑謂家人：「吾將種白蓮於此，此花出泥淖無所染，令亡者知予心耳。」

translations.literal: One day the wife ordered a pit dug before the bed curtain to bury a great jar of water, and smiling told the family: "I shall plant white lotus here—this flower rises from the mud yet is unstained, so the dead may know my heart."
translations.idiomatic: One day the wife ordered a pit dug before the bed curtain to bury a great jar of water, and smiling told the family, "I shall plant white lotus here—this flower rises from the mud yet is unstained, so the dead may know my heart."

sentences.zh: 於是日纂輯不懈。

translations.literal: Thereafter she compiled daily without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she compiled daily without slackening.

sentences.zh: 書將成，防者稍不戒，則濡首缸中死矣。

translations.literal: When the book was nearly done, the watchers relaxed their vigil somewhat, and she drowned her head in the jar and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was nearly done, the watchers relaxed their vigil somewhat, and she drowned her head in the jar and died.

sentences.zh: 為文脫稿即毀，所存《列女傳》及《哭夫文》四篇、《夢夫賦》一篇，皆文止竊而得之者。

translations.literal: Her writings were destroyed as soon as drafts were finished; the surviving "Biographies of Exemplary Women," four "Lament for My Husband" pieces, and one "Rhapsody Dreaming of My Husband" were all secretly obtained by Wenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Her writings were destroyed as soon as drafts were finished; the surviving Biographies of Exemplary Women, four Laments for My Husband, and one Rhapsody Dreaming of My Husband were all secretly obtained by Wenzhi.

sentences.zh: 御史聞於朝，榜其門曰文章貞節。

translations.literal: The censor reported it at court and an archway was erected over her gate reading "Literary Fidelity and Chaste Constancy."
translations.idiomatic: The censor reported it at court, and an archway was erected over her gate reading "Literary Fidelity and Chaste Constancy."

sentences.zh: 初，其兄見女能文，以李易安、朱淑真比之，輒嚬蹙曰：「易安更嫁，而淑真不慊其夫，雖能文，大節虧矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when her elder brother saw the girl could write, he compared her to Li Yi'an and Zhu Shuzhen; she would always frown and say: "Yi'an remarried, and Shuzhen was discontent with her husband—though they could write, great integrity was lacking."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when her elder brother saw the girl could write and compared her to Li Yi'an and Zhu Shuzhen, she would always frown and say, "Yi'an remarried, and Shuzhen was discontent with her husband—though they could write, their great integrity was lacking."

sentences.zh: 其幼時誌操已如此。

translations.literal: Even in youth her resolution was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Even in youth her resolution was thus.

sentences.zh: 楊玉英，建寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Yuying was from Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuying was from Jianning.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書史，善吟詠。

translations.literal: She read widely in books and histories and was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: She read widely in books and histories and was skilled in poetry.

sentences.zh: 年十八，許字官時中。

translations.literal: At eighteen she was betrothed to Guan Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she was betrothed to Guan Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 時中有非意之獄，父母改受他聘。

translations.literal: Shizhong was caught in an unjust case; her parents accepted another betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong was caught in an unjust case; her parents accepted another betrothal.

sentences.zh: 玉英聞之，囑其婢曰：「吾篋有佩囊、布鞵諸物，異日以遺官官人。」

translations.literal: When Yuying heard of it, she told her maid: "In my chest are a sachet, cloth shoes, and other things—on another day give them to Master Guan."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuying heard of it, she told her maid, "In my chest are a sachet, cloth shoes, and other things—on another day give them to Master Guan."

sentences.zh: 婢弗悟，諸之。

translations.literal: The maid did not understand and questioned her.
translations.idiomatic: The maid did not understand and questioned her.

sentences.zh: 於是竊入寢室，自經死，目不瞑。

translations.literal: She then stole into her bedroom and hanged herself; her eyes would not close.
translations.idiomatic: She then stole into her bedroom and hanged herself; her eyes would not close.

sentences.zh: 時中聞訃，具禮往祭，以手掩之，遂瞑。

translations.literal: When Shizhong heard the death notice, he went with full rites to mourn; he covered them with his hand, and they closed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong heard the death notice, he went with full rites to mourn; he covered them with his hand, and they closed.

sentences.zh: 婢出所遺物，付父母啟之，得詩云：「昆山一片玉，既售與卞和。
