translations.literal: The maid brought out the bequeathed items for her parents to open; they found a poem saying: "A piece of jade from Kunshan—once sold to Bian He.
translations.idiomatic: The maid brought out the bequeathed items for her parents to open; they found a poem saying, "A piece of jade from Kunshan—once sold to Bian He.

sentences.zh: 和足苦被刖，玉堅不可磨。

translations.literal: He suffered the cutting off of his feet in anguish—the jade is hard and cannot be ground away.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered the cutting off of his feet in anguish—the jade is hard and cannot be ground away.

sentences.zh: 若再付他人，其如平生何！」

translations.literal: If it were given to another man—how would that honor our shared life!"
translations.idiomatic: If it were given to another man—how would that honor our shared life!"

sentences.zh: 又張蟬雲，蒲城人，許字俞檜。

translations.literal: Also Zhang Chanyun of Pucheng was betrothed to Yu Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Also Zhang Chanyun of Pucheng was betrothed to Yu Hui.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，檜被誣繫獄。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign, Hui was falsely accused and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Hui was falsely accused and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 女聞可賄脫，謀諸母，欲貨妝奩助之。

translations.literal: The girl heard he could be released by bribery and discussed with her mother a plan to sell her dowry to help.
translations.idiomatic: The girl heard he could be released by bribery and discussed with her mother a plan to sell her dowry to help.

sentences.zh: 母不可，曰：「汝未嫁，何為若此。」

translations.literal: Her mother refused, saying: "You are not yet married—why act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother refused, saying, "You are not yet married—why act thus?"

sentences.zh: 女方食，即以碗擲地，恚不語。

translations.literal: While the girl was eating, she threw her bowl to the floor, angry and silent.
translations.idiomatic: While the girl was eating, she threw her bowl to the floor, angry and silent.

sentences.zh: 入暮自縊死。

translations.literal: At dusk she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 陳襄妻倪氏。

translations.literal: Ni, wife of Chen Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ni, wife of Chen Xiang.

sentences.zh: 襄為鄞諸生，早卒。

translations.literal: Xiang was a licentiate of Yin and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a licentiate of Yin and died young.

sentences.zh: 婦年三十，無子，家貧，力女紅養姑。

translations.literal: The wife was thirty, childless, and poor; she worked needlework to support her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The wife was thirty, childless, and poor; she worked needlework to support her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 有慕其姿者，遣媒白姑。

translations.literal: Someone who admired her beauty sent a matchmaker to tell the mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who admired her beauty sent a matchmaker to tell the mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 婦煎沸湯自漬其面，左目爆出，又以煙煤塗傷處，遂成獰惡狀。

translations.literal: The wife boiled water and scalded her own face; her left eye burst out; she also smeared coal dust on the wounds until she had a hideous appearance.
translations.idiomatic: The wife boiled water and scalded her own face; her left eye burst out; she also smeared coal dust on the wounds until she had a hideous appearance.

sentences.zh: 媒過之，驚走，不敢復以聘告。

translations.literal: When the matchmaker passed by she fled in alarm and dared not mention marriage again.
translations.idiomatic: When the matchmaker passed by she fled in alarm and dared not mention marriage again.

sentences.zh: 歷二十年，姑壽七十餘卒，婦哀慟不食死。

translations.literal: After twenty years the mother-in-law died in her seventies; the wife grieved and refused food until she died.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years the mother-in-law died in her seventies; the wife grieved and refused food until she died.

sentences.zh: 彭氏，安丘人。

translations.literal: Peng was from Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Peng was from Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 幼字王枚臯。

translations.literal: From youth she was betrothed to Wang Meigao.
translations.idiomatic: From youth she was betrothed to Wang Meigao.

sentences.zh: 未嫁，枚臯卒，誓不再適。

translations.literal: Before marriage Meigao died; she vowed never to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Before marriage Meigao died; she vowed never to remarry.

sentences.zh: 濰縣丁道平密囑其父欲娶之。

translations.literal: Ding Daoping of Weixian secretly told her father he wished to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Daoping of Weixian secretly told her father he wished to marry her.

sentences.zh: 彭察知，六日不食。

translations.literal: Peng learned of it and ate nothing for six days.
translations.idiomatic: Peng learned of it and ate nothing for six days.

sentences.zh: 道平悔而止，心敬女節烈，後聞其疾革不起，贈以棺。

translations.literal: Daoping regretted and stopped; he respected her chaste integrity and later, hearing she was gravely ill and would not recover, sent her a coffin as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Daoping regretted and stopped; he respected her chaste integrity, and later, hearing she was gravely ill and would not recover, sent her a coffin as a gift.

sentences.zh: 彭語父曰：「可束葦埋我，亟還丁氏棺，地下欲見王枚臯也。」

translations.literal: Peng told her father: "You may bind reeds to bury me—return Ding's coffin at once; below ground I wish to meet Wang Meigao."
translations.idiomatic: Peng told her father, "You may bind reeds to bury me—return Ding's coffin at once; below ground I wish to meet Wang Meigao."

sentences.zh: 遂死。

translations.literal: Then she died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she died.

sentences.zh: 又劉氏，潁州劉梅女，許聘李之本。

translations.literal: Also Liu, daughter of Liu Mei of Yingzhou, betrothed to Li Zhiben.
translations.idiomatic: Also Lady Liu, daughter of Liu Mei of Yingzhou, was betrothed to Li Zhiben.

sentences.zh: 之本歿，女泣血不食，語父曰：「兒為李郎服三年，需弟稍長，然後殉。

translations.literal: When Zhiben died, the girl wept blood and refused food, telling her father: "Your daughter will mourn Li for three years; when my younger brother is grown a little, then I shall die with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiben died, the girl wept blood and refused food, telling her father, "Your daughter will mourn Li for three years; when my younger brother is grown a little, then I shall die with him.

sentences.zh: 寄語翁，且勿為郎置槨。」

translations.literal: Tell the old gentleman not yet to prepare a coffin for him."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the old gentleman not yet to prepare a coffin for him."

sentences.zh: 遂盡去鉛華，教弟讀書，親正句讀。

translations.literal: She then put aside all cosmetics, taught her brother to read, and personally corrected his parsing of passages.
translations.idiomatic: She then put aside all cosmetics, taught her brother to read, and personally corrected his parsing of passages.

sentences.zh: 越一年，梅潛許田家。

translations.literal: After a year Mei secretly betrothed her to the Tian clan.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Mei secretly betrothed her to the Tian clan.

sentences.zh: 女聞，中夜開篋，取李幣，挑燈制衣，衣之，縊死。

translations.literal: When the girl heard, in the middle of the night she opened her chest, took out Li's betrothal gifts, sewed garments by lamplight, put them on, and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When the girl heard, in the middle of the night she opened her chest, took out Li's betrothal gifts, sewed garments by lamplight, put them on, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 知府謝詔臨其喪，鄰里吊者如市。

translations.literal: The prefect Xie Zhao attended her funeral; neighbors who came to mourn were as numerous as a market.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xie Zhao came to her funeral, and mourners from the neighborhood filled the streets like a market fair.

sentences.zh: 田家亦具奠賻，舉酒方酹，柩前承灌瓦盆劃然而碎，起高丈餘，繞檐如蝶墜。

translations.literal: The Tian family also prepared offerings and condolence gifts. As they raised wine to pour a libation, the earthenware basin receiving the pour before the coffin suddenly cracked apart, rose more than ten feet high, and circled the eaves like butterflies alighting.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian family brought offerings and gifts as well. Just as they raised wine to pour a libation, the earthen basin before the coffin that caught the offering shattered with a sharp crack, flew more than ten feet into the air, and drifted around the eaves before falling like butterflies.

sentences.zh: 觀者震色。

translations.literal: Those watching changed color in shock.
translations.idiomatic: The onlookers went pale with shock.

sentences.zh: 劉氏二孝女，汝陽人。

translations.literal: The two filial daughters of the Liu clan were from Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: The two filial daughters of the Liu family were from Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 父玉生七女，家貧力田。

translations.literal: Their father Yu had seven daughters; the family was poor and farmed by labor.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Yu had seven daughters. The family was poor and worked the fields themselves.

sentences.zh: 嘗至隴上，嘆曰：「生女不生男，使我扶犁不輟。」

translations.literal: Once when he went to the field ridge, he sighed and said, "Having daughters and not sons makes me never cease guiding the plow."
translations.idiomatic: Once on the ridge between the fields, he sighed and said, "Daughters instead of sons—so I must keep to the plow without rest."

sentences.zh: 其第四、第六女聞之惻然，誓不嫁，著短衣代父耕作。

translations.literal: His fourth and sixth daughters, hearing this, were deeply moved; they vowed not to marry, put on short garments, and farmed in their father's place.
translations.idiomatic: When the fourth and sixth daughters heard this, their hearts were moved. They vowed never to marry, dressed in short work clothes, and took over the farming for their father.

sentences.zh: 及父母相繼卒，無力營葬，二女即屋為丘，不離親側。

translations.literal: When father and mother died one after another, they had no strength to arrange burial; the two daughters made their house into a mound and did not leave their parents' side.
translations.idiomatic: When their parents died in succession and they could not afford a proper burial, the two sisters turned their home into a burial mound and never left their parents' side.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，督學副使楊俊民、知府史桂芳詣其舍請見，二女年皆逾六十矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing, Education Intendant Vice Commissioner Yang Junmin and Prefect Shi Guifang went to their dwelling to request an audience; both daughters were already over sixty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Longqing reign, Education Intendant Yang Junmin and Prefect Shi Guifang came to their home seeking an audience—and both sisters were already over sixty.

sentences.zh: 黃氏，江寧陳伯妻。

translations.literal: Lady Huang was the wife of Chen Bo of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huang was the wife of Chen Bo of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 年十八，歸伯。

translations.literal: At eighteen she was married to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she married Bo.

sentences.zh: 父死，母欲改節，氏苦諫不從。

translations.literal: When her father died, her mother wished to remarry; Lady Huang earnestly remonstrated but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: After her father died, her mother wished to remarry. Lady Huang pleaded with her earnestly but could not dissuade her.

sentences.zh: 一日，母來省，女閉門不與相見，母慚去。

translations.literal: One day her mother came to visit; the daughter closed the door and would not meet her; the mother left in shame.
translations.idiomatic: One day when her mother came to visit, the daughter shut the door and refused to see her. Her mother withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 後伯疾篤，黃誓不獨生。

translations.literal: Later Bo's illness became grave; Huang vowed not to live alone.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Bo fell mortally ill, Huang vowed she would not survive him.

sentences.zh: 一日，姑扶伯起坐，黃熟視曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: One day the mother-in-law helped Bo sit up; Huang gazed intently and said, "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: One day, as her mother-in-law helped Bo sit up, Huang looked closely at him and said, "Ah—

sentences.zh: 病至此，吾無望矣。」

translations.literal: The illness has reached this point—I have no hope left."
translations.idiomatic: the illness has come to this. I have no hope left."

sentences.zh: 走竈下，碎食器刺喉不殊，以廚刀自刎死，年二十一。

translations.literal: She ran beneath the stove, smashed an eating vessel and stabbed her throat without success, then cut her own throat with a kitchen knife and died, aged twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: She ran to the kitchen, smashed a dish and stabbed at her throat without effect, then took a kitchen knife and cut her own throat. She was twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 邵氏，丹陽大俠邵方家婢也。

translations.literal: Lady Shao was a maidservant in the household of the great hero Shao Fang of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shao was a servant in the household of Shao Fang, a renowned swashbuckler of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 方子儀，令婢視之。

translations.literal: Fang had a son Yi; he had the maidservant nurse him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had a son named Yi, whom he entrusted to the maid to raise.

sentences.zh: 故相徐階、高拱並家居，方以策幹階，階不用，即走謁拱，為營復相，名傾中外。

translations.literal: The former grand secretaries Xu Jie and Gao Gong were both living at home; Fang used schemes to approach Jie, but Jie did not employ him, so he immediately went to pay court to Gong; Gong restored him to the post of grand secretary, and his fame shook court and country.
translations.idiomatic: Former chief ministers Xu Jie and Gao Gong were both retired at home. Shao Fang tried to win Xu Jie's favor with schemes, but Xu would have none of it. Fang then went to Gao Gong, who helped restore him to the chief ministership, making his name resound throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，拱罷，張居正屬巡撫張佳胤捕殺方，並逮儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Gong was dismissed; Zhang Juzheng ordered Grand Coordinator Zhang Jiayin to capture and kill Fang, and also seized Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, after Gao Gong was dismissed, Zhang Juzheng ordered Grand Coordinator Zhang Jiayin to capture and kill Shao Fang and take Yi into custody as well.

sentences.zh: 儀甫三歲，捕者以日暮未發，閉方所居宅，守之。

translations.literal: Yi was only three years old; the captors, because dusk had come, did not yet set out; they shut the residence where Fang lived and kept watch over it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was only three years old. The arrest party, delayed by nightfall, sealed Shao Fang's house and posted guards.

sentences.zh: 方女夫武進沈應奎，義烈士，負氣有力，時為諸生，念儀死，邵氏絕，將往救之。

translations.literal: Fang's son-in-law Shen Yingkui of Wujin was a righteous hero, proud-spirited and strong; he was then a licentiate; thinking that if Yi died the line of Shao would end, he intended to go save him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's son-in-law Shen Yingkui of Wujin was a man of fierce loyalty and great strength, then a student at the imperial academy. He feared that if Yi were killed, the Shao line would be extinguished, and resolved to rescue the boy.

sentences.zh: 而府推官與應奎善，固邀飲，夜分乃罷。

translations.literal: But the prefecture's assistant magistrate was on good terms with Yingkui and firmly invited him to drink; only at midnight did they finish.
translations.idiomatic: But a magistrate's assistant who was Yingkui's friend insisted on keeping him at wine, and they did not part until the middle of the night.

sentences.zh: 武進距方居五十里，應奎逾城出，夜半抵方家，逾墻入，婢方坐燈下，抱儀泣曰：「安得沈郎來，屬以此子。」

translations.literal: Wujin was fifty li from Fang's residence; Yingkui scaled the city wall and went out; at midnight he reached Fang's house, climbed over the wall and entered; the maidservant was sitting under the lamp, holding Yi and weeping, saying, "If only Master Shen would come—I could entrust this child to him."
translations.idiomatic: Wujin was fifty li from Fang's house. Yingkui climbed over the city wall and by midnight reached the Shao residence. He scaled the wall and found the maid sitting by lamplight, holding Yi and weeping: "If only Shen could come—I would entrust this child to him."

sentences.zh: 應奎倉卒前，婢立以儀授之，頓首曰：「邵氏之祀在君矣。

translations.literal: Yingkui hastily stepped forward; the maid stood and handed Yi to him, kowtowed, and said, "The sacrifices of the Shao clan now rest with you.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui stepped forward without warning. The maid rose and placed Yi in his arms, then kowtowed and said, "The continuation of the Shao line is now in your hands.

sentences.zh: 此子生，婢死無憾。」

translations.literal: If this child lives, I die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: If this child lives, I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 應奎匿儀去，晨謁推官。

translations.literal: Yingkui hid Yi and left; in the morning he paid a visit to the assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui concealed Yi and fled. At dawn he called on the assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 旦日，捕者失儀，系婢毒掠，終無言。

translations.literal: The next morning the captors found Yi gone; they bound the maidservant and tortured her severely, but she never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the arrest party discovered Yi missing. They bound the maid and tortured her brutally, but she never said a word.

sentences.zh: 或言於守曰：「必應奎匿之。」

translations.literal: Someone said to the prefect, "Yingkui must be hiding him."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the prefect, "Yingkui must be the one hiding him."

sentences.zh: 奎所善推官在坐，大笑曰：「冤哉！

translations.literal: The assistant magistrate who was Yingkui's friend was present and laughed loudly, saying, "What a grievous injustice!
translations.idiomatic: The assistant magistrate who was Yingkui's friend was seated nearby and laughed aloud: "What an injustice!

sentences.zh: 應奎夜飲於余，晨又謁余也。」

translations.literal: Yingkui drank at my place last night, and this morning visited me as well."
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui drank at my house last night and came to see me again this morning."

sentences.zh: 會有為方解者，事乃寢，婢撫其子以老。

translations.literal: Just then someone interceded for Fang; the matter then subsided; the maidservant raised the child until old age.
translations.idiomatic: Just then someone pleaded on Fang's behalf, and the matter was dropped. The maid raised the child to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 楊貞婦，潼關衛人，字郭恒。

translations.literal: The chaste wife Yang was from Tongguan Guard; she was betrothed to Guo Heng.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste wife Yang, of Tongguan Guard, was betrothed to Guo Heng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，客遊湖南，久不歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, as a traveling guest he went to Hunan and for a long time did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, Heng traveled to Hunan as a visitor and did not return for many years.

sentences.zh: 父議納他聘，女不可，斷發自守。

translations.literal: Her father discussed accepting another betrothal; the daughter refused, cut her hair, and kept her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Her father considered arranging another match. The daughter refused, cropped her hair, and held to her vow.

sentences.zh: 家有巖壁，穴墻居之，垂橐以通飲食，如是者二十六年。

translations.literal: The family had a rock wall; she hollowed the wall and lived inside; a pouch was lowered for passing food and drink—in this way for twenty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: At home there was a cliff face. She hollowed out a cell in the rock and lived there, receiving food and drink through a pouch lowered from above—for twenty-six years.

sentences.zh: 恒歸，乃成禮。

translations.literal: When Heng returned, they then completed the marriage rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng at last returned, they were married.

sentences.zh: 又有倪氏，歸安人，許聘陳敏。

translations.literal: There was also the Ni clan; from Gui'an; betrothed to Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Ni of Gui'an, betrothed to Chen Min.

sentences.zh: 敏從征，傳為已死。

translations.literal: Min followed a military campaign; it was reported that he had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Min went off on campaign, and word came that he had died.

sentences.zh: 逾五十載始歸。

translations.literal: After more than fifty years he finally returned.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty years passed before he returned.

sentences.zh: 倪守志不嫁，至是成婚，年六十一矣。

translations.literal: Ni kept her vow and did not marry; only then did they complete the marriage; she was sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: Ni had kept her vow and never remarried. They married at last—she was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 楊氏，寧國饒鼎妻。

translations.literal: Lady Yang was the wife of Rao Ding of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was the wife of Rao Ding of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 鼎以單衣溺死湖中，楊招魂葬之，課二子成立，冬不衣袷。

translations.literal: Ding drowned in the lake wearing only a single garment; Yang summoned his soul and buried him, instructed the two sons until they were established, and in winter wore no padded coat.
translations.idiomatic: Ding drowned in the lake wearing only a thin garment. Yang performed rites to summon his soul and gave him burial, raised their two sons to maturity, and wore no padded coat even in winter.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，年八十，竟單衣入宅旁池中，端坐死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, aged eighty, she finally entered the pool beside the residence wearing only a single garment and died sitting upright.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, at eighty, she entered the pond beside her home dressed only in a thin robe and died sitting upright in the water.

sentences.zh: 丁氏，五河王序禮妻。

translations.literal: Lady Ding was the wife of Wang Xuli of Wuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding was the wife of Wang Xuli of Wuhe.

sentences.zh: 序禮弟序爵客外，為賊所殺，其妻郭氏懷孕未即殉。

translations.literal: Xuli's younger brother Xujue was a traveling guest abroad and was killed by bandits; his wife Lady Guo was pregnant and did not immediately follow him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Xuli's younger brother Xujue was killed by bandits while traveling. His wife Lady Guo was pregnant and could not yet die with him.

sentences.zh: 及生子越月，投繯死。

translations.literal: After giving birth, a month later she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: A month after giving birth, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 時丁氏適生女，泣謂序禮曰：「叔不幸客死，嬸復殉，棄孤不養，責在君與妾也。

translations.literal: At that time Lady Ding had just given birth to a daughter; weeping she said to Xuli, "Our uncle-unfortunately died abroad; our aunt-in-law also followed him in death; to abandon the orphan and not raise him—the responsibility rests with you and me.
translations.idiomatic: Ding had just given birth to a daughter. Weeping, she told Xuli, "Your brother died far from home, and his wife has followed him in death. If we abandon this orphan, the blame will be ours.

sentences.zh: 妾初舉女，後尚有期，孤亡則斬叔之嗣，且負嬸矣。」

translations.literal: I have just borne a daughter; there may yet be more children; if the orphan dies it cuts off my brother-in-law's line and fails his wife as well."
translations.idiomatic: I have just had a daughter, and there may be more children to come. If this orphan dies, your brother's line ends—and I fail his wife as well."

sentences.zh: 遂棄女乳侄。

translations.literal: She then abandoned the daughter and nursed the nephew.
translations.idiomatic: She then set aside her own daughter and nursed the nephew instead.

sentences.zh: 未幾，序禮亦死，竟無子女。

translations.literal: Before long Xuli also died; in the end there were no children.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xuli died too, and in the end they had no children of their own.

sentences.zh: 氏年方少，撫侄長，絕無怨悔。

translations.literal: Lady Ding was still young; she raised the nephew to adulthood and never had resentment or regret.
translations.idiomatic: Though still young, Ding raised the boy to manhood without a trace of bitterness or regret.

sentences.zh: 尤氏，昆山貢生鏞女。

translations.literal: Lady You was the daughter of the tribute student Yong of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady You was the daughter of Yong, a tribute student of Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 嫁諸生趙一鳳，早死，將殉之，顧二子方繈褓，為強食。

translations.literal: She married the licentiate Zhao Yifeng; he died early; she intended to follow him in death, but seeing the two sons still in swaddling clothes, she forced herself to eat.
translations.idiomatic: She married the scholar Zhao Yifeng, who died young. She meant to die with him, but her two sons were still infants, so she forced herself to eat and live.

sentences.zh: 二子復殤，慟曰：「可以從夫矣。」

translations.literal: Both sons also died young; grieving she said, "Now I can follow my husband."
translations.idiomatic: When both sons died in infancy, she grieved: "Now I can join my husband."

sentences.zh: 痛夫未葬，即營窀穸。

translations.literal: Grieving that her husband was not yet buried, she immediately prepared the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband had not yet been buried; she immediately set about preparing his tomb.

sentences.zh: 惡少年艷其色，訾其目曰：「彼盼美而流，烏能久也。」

translations.literal: A wicked youth lusting after her beauty sneered at her eyes and said, "Those seductive glances flowing about—how could she last long!"
translations.idiomatic: A vicious young man, taken with her beauty, mocked her eyes: "Those come-hither glances—she won't hold out long."

sentences.zh: 婦聞之，夜取石灰手挼目，血出立枯。

translations.literal: When the wife heard this, that night she took lime and rubbed her eyes by hand; blood flowed and they immediately withered.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard this, she took lime that night and rubbed it into her eyes until blood ran and they shriveled at once.

sentences.zh: 置棺自隨。

translations.literal: She kept a coffin with her at all times.
translations.idiomatic: She kept a coffin ready beside her at all times.

sentences.zh: 夫葬畢，即自縊，或解之，乃觸石裂額，趨臥棺中死。

translations.literal: When her husband's burial was complete, she immediately hanged herself; when someone untied her, she then struck a stone and split her forehead, rushed to lie in the coffin and died.
translations.idiomatic: Once her husband was buried, she hanged herself. When someone cut her down, she dashed her forehead against a stone, then flung herself into the coffin and died.

sentences.zh: 李氏，王寵麟繼妻。

translations.literal: Lady Li was the second wife of Wang Chonglin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was the second wife of Wang Chonglin.

sentences.zh: 寵麟仕知府卒，氏年二十餘，哭泣不食，經四十日疾革。

translations.literal: Chonglin served as prefect and died; Lady Li was a little over twenty; she wept and would not eat; after forty days her illness became critical.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglin died while serving as prefect. Li was barely twenty. She wept and refused food until, after forty days, she lay near death.

sentences.zh: 知族人利其資，必以惡語傾前妻子，預戒家人置己棺中，勿封殮。

translations.literal: Knowing that clansmen coveted their property and would certainly use slander to ruin the former wife's son, she beforehand warned her family to place her in a coffin without sealing the encoffinment.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing her kinsmen coveted the estate and would slander her stepson, she told her family in advance to place her in a coffin but leave it unsealed.

sentences.zh: 眾果猬集，噪孤殺母。

translations.literal: The crowd indeed gathered like hedgehogs, clamoring that the orphan had killed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The relatives crowded in as expected, shouting that the boy had murdered his mother.

sentences.zh: 氏從棺中言：「已知汝輩計必出此也。」

translations.literal: Lady Li spoke from inside the coffin: "I already knew your scheme would certainly produce this."
translations.idiomatic: From inside the coffin Li spoke: "I knew you would stoop to this."

sentences.zh: 眾大慚而去，然後瞑。

translations.literal: The crowd was greatly ashamed and left; only then did she close her eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The relatives slunk away in shame. Only then did she close her eyes for the last time.

sentences.zh: 孫氏，甌寧人。

translations.literal: Lady Sun was from Ouning.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sun was from Ouning.

sentences.zh: 幼解經史，字吳廷桂。

translations.literal: From youth she understood the classics and histories; she was betrothed to Wu Tinggui.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she knew the classics and histories. She was betrothed to Wu Tinggui.

sentences.zh: 廷桂死，孫欲左喪，家人止不得，父為命輿。

translations.literal: Tinggui died; Sun wished to take the left side of mourning; her family stopped her and could not; her father ordered a sedan chair for her.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinggui died, Sun wished to join him in death, but her family would not allow it. Her father ordered a sedan chair for her.

sentences.zh: 曰：「奔喪而輿，可乎？」

translations.literal: She said, "Rushing to mourning yet riding a sedan—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Can one rush to a funeral riding in a sedan?"

sentences.zh: 入夜，徒步往，挾納采雙金雀以見舅姑。

translations.literal: At night she went on foot, carrying the pair of golden sparrows from the betrothal gifts to meet her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: That night she went on foot, bearing the pair of golden sparrows from the betrothal rites to present herself to her in-laws.

sentences.zh: 拜畢，奠柩側，遂不離次，期必死。

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, she made offerings beside the coffin and then never left her mourning station, set on dying.
translations.idiomatic: After paying her respects, she made offerings beside the coffin and never left the bier, determined to die.

sentences.zh: 吳家故貧，所治棺，取具而已。

translations.literal: The Wu family was originally poor; the coffin they prepared was merely adequate.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu family was poor; the coffin they had prepared was barely sufficient.

sentences.zh: 好事者助以美槚，孫視之曰：「木以美逾吾夫，非禮矣。」

translations.literal: Well-wishers contributed fine coffin wood; Sun looked at it and said, "Wood more fine than my husband deserves is not proper ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Sympathizers offered fine coffin wood. Sun looked at it and said, "Wood finer than my husband deserves violates propriety."

sentences.zh: 卻之。

translations.literal: She refused it.
translations.idiomatic: She declined it.

sentences.zh: 以槥櫝來，乃許。

translations.literal: When a plain coffin came, she then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When a plain coffin was offered, she accepted.

sentences.zh: 屆期縊死，書衣帶中云：「男毋附屍，女毋啟衣。」

translations.literal: When the appointed day arrived she hanged herself; in her sash she wrote: "Men must not attach themselves to the corpse; women must not lift the shroud."
translations.idiomatic: When the day came she hanged herself. In her sash she left a note: "Let no man cling to my corpse; let no woman lift my shroud."

sentences.zh: 方孝女，莆田人。

translations.literal: The filial daughter Fang was from Putian.
translations.idiomatic: The filial daughter Fang was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 父瀾，官儀制郎中，卒京師。

translations.literal: Her father Lan served as Bureau Director of Ceremonial Regulations and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Lan, Director of Ceremonial Regulations, died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 女年十四，無他兄弟，與叔父扶櫬歸。

translations.literal: The daughter was fourteen; she had no other brothers; with her uncle she escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: The girl was fourteen, with no other brothers. She and her uncle escorted the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 渡揚子江，中流舟覆，櫬浮。

translations.literal: Crossing the Yangzi River, midstream the boat capsized; the coffin floated.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yangzi, the boat capsized midstream. The coffin floated free.

sentences.zh: 女時居別舟，皇遽呼救，風濤洶怒，人莫敢前。

translations.literal: The daughter was then in a separate boat; in panic she called for help; wind and waves were furious and no one dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: The girl was in another boat. Desperately she called for help, but the wind and waves raged and no one dared approach.

sentences.zh: 女仰天大哭，遂赴水死。

translations.literal: The daughter looked heavenward and wailed greatly, then threw herself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The girl raised her face to heaven and wailed, then plunged into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 經三日，屍浮，傍父櫬，同泊南岸。

translations.literal: After three days the corpse floated up beside her father's coffin; both came to rest on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later her body rose to the surface beside her father's coffin. Both drifted to the south bank together.

sentences.zh: 又有解孝女，寧陵人。

translations.literal: There was also the filial daughter Xie, from Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the filial daughter Xie of Ningling.

sentences.zh: 年十四，同母浣衣。

translations.literal: Aged fourteen, she was washing clothes with her mother.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she was washing clothes with her mother.

sentences.zh: 母誤溺水，女四顧無人，號泣投水。

translations.literal: Her mother accidentally fell into the water and drowned; the daughter looked around and found no one; wailing she threw herself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother slipped into the water. Finding no one nearby, the girl wailed and jumped in after her.

sentences.zh: 俄兄紹武至，泅而得之，母女皆死。

translations.literal: Soon her elder brother Shaowu arrived, swam and recovered them; mother and daughter both were dead.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Shaowu arrived moments later. He swam out and pulled them ashore—but mother and daughter were both lifeless.

sentences.zh: 女手挽母甚堅，兄救母，久之復蘇。

translations.literal: The daughter's hand grasping her mother was very firm; the brother saved the mother, and after a long while she revived.
translations.idiomatic: The girl's grip on her mother was iron-strong. The brother revived the mother, who after a long while came back to consciousness.

sentences.zh: 女手仍不解，兄哭撫之曰：「母已生，妹可慰矣。」

translations.literal: The daughter's hand still would not release; the brother wept and comforted her, saying, "Mother is alive—little sister, you may take comfort now."
translations.idiomatic: The girl's grip would not loosen. Her brother wept and said, "Mother lives—little sister, you may rest now."

sentences.zh: 乃解。

translations.literal: Only then did she release.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did she let go.

sentences.zh: 李氏，東鄉何璇妻。

translations.literal: Lady Li was the wife of He Xuan of Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was the wife of He Xuan of Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 璇客死。

translations.literal: Xuan died abroad as a traveling guest.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died far from home.

sentences.zh: 李有殊色，父迫之嫁。

translations.literal: Li had exceptional beauty; her father pressured her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Li was strikingly beautiful. Her father pressed her to marry again.

sentences.zh: 遂以簪入耳中，手自拳之至沒，復拔出，血濺如註。

translations.literal: She then thrust a hairpin into her ear, pushing with her hand until it was submerged, then pulled it out again; blood splashed like pouring.
translations.idiomatic: She drove a hairpin into her ear, pushing it in with her fist until it disappeared, then pulled it out again. Blood gushed as if from a fountain.

sentences.zh: 姑覺，呼家人救，則已死矣。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law noticed, called the family to save her, but she was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law noticed and called for help, but Li was already dead.

sentences.zh: 項貞女，秀水人。

translations.literal: The chaste daughter Xiang was from Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste daughter Xiang was from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 國子生道亨女，字吳江周應祁。

translations.literal: Daughter of the Imperial Academy student Daoheng; betrothed to Zhou Yingqi of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of the academy student Daoheng, betrothed to Zhou Yingqi of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 精女工，解琴瑟，通《列女傳》，事祖母及母極孝。

translations.literal: She excelled at women's handicraft, understood the zither and se, was versed in the "Biographies of Exemplary Women," and served her grandmother and mother with the utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She was skilled in needlework, played the zither and se, knew the Biographies of Exemplary Women by heart, and served her grandmother and mother with extraordinary devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十九，聞周病瘵，即持齋、燃香燈禮佛，默有所祝，侍女輩竊聽，微聞以身代語。

translations.literal: At age nineteen, upon hearing that Zhou was ill with consumption, she immediately observed abstinence, lit incense lamps, and worshipped Buddha, silently making a prayer; the maidservants secretly listened and faintly heard words about offering her own body in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When she was nineteen and learned that Zhou was wasting away with illness, she at once began fasting, lit incense before the Buddha, and prayed in silence. The maidservants listened in secret and faintly caught her vowing to give her own life in his stead.

sentences.zh: 一日，謂乳媼曰：「未嫁而夫亡，當奈何？」

translations.literal: One day she said to her wet nurse: "Not yet married and the husband dies—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: One day she asked her wet nurse, "If I have not yet married and my betrothed dies, what am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「未成婦，改字無害。」

translations.literal: The nurse said: "Having not yet become a wife, changing the betrothal would do no harm."
translations.idiomatic: The nurse answered, "You are not yet a wife—there would be no harm in breaking the engagement."

sentences.zh: 女正容曰：「昔賢以一劍許人，猶不忍負，況身乎？」

translations.literal: The girl set her countenance and said: "In olden days a worthy man promised a sword to someone and still could not bear to go back on his word—how much more so with one's own person?"
translations.idiomatic: The girl composed her face and said, "Men of old would promise even a sword to someone and could not bear to break their word—how much more binding is a pledge of one's own person?"

sentences.zh: 及訃聞，父母秘其事，然傳吳江人來，女已喻。

translations.literal: When the death notice arrived, her parents kept the matter secret; yet word came that people from Wujiang had arrived, and the girl already understood.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death arrived, her parents tried to keep it from her—but before the messenger from Wujiang even arrived, the girl already knew.

sentences.zh: 祖母屬其母入視，女留母坐，色甚溫，母釋然去。

translations.literal: Her grandmother told her mother to go in and look in on her; the girl kept her mother seated; her expression was very gentle; her mother departed reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandmother sent her mother in to check on her. The girl kept her mother sitting with her, her manner gentle and warm. Her mother left reassured.

sentences.zh: 夜伺諸婢熟睡，獨起以素絲約發，衣內外悉易以縞，而紉其下裳。

translations.literal: At night, waiting until the maids were sound asleep, she rose alone, bound her hair with plain silk, changed all her inner and outer garments to white hemp mourning cloth, and stitched her lower skirt.
translations.idiomatic: That night she waited until the maids were deep asleep, then rose alone. She bound her hair with white silk, dressed herself entirely in hemp mourning garb, and stitched her skirt closed.

sentences.zh: 檢衣物當勞諸婢者，名標之，列諸床上。

translations.literal: She sorted out clothing that should serve as gifts for the maids, labeled each by name, and laid them out on the bed.
translations.idiomatic: She set aside garments as tokens of thanks for each maid, labeled them by name, and laid them in a row upon her bed.

sentences.zh: 大書於幾曰：「上告父母，兒不得奉一日，今為周郎死矣。」

translations.literal: She wrote in large characters on the table: "Reporting to my parents above: your daughter could not serve you for even one day; now she dies for Master Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: On her table she wrote in large characters: "To my parents above: your daughter never served you even one day—and now she dies for Zhou."

sentences.zh: 遂自縊。

translations.literal: Then she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Then she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 兩家父母從其志，竟合葬焉。

translations.literal: The parents of both families followed her wish and in the end buried them together.
translations.idiomatic: Both families honored her wish and buried her beside Zhou in a joint grave.

sentences.zh: 李氏，壽昌人。

translations.literal: Lady Li was from Shouchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was from Shouchang.

sentences.zh: 年十三，受翁應兆聘。

translations.literal: At age thirteen she received betrothal from Ying Zhao of the Weng clan.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she was betrothed to Ying Zhao of the Weng family.

sentences.zh: 應兆暴卒，女盡取備嫁衣飾焚之，以身赴火，為父母救止。

translations.literal: Ying Zhao died suddenly; the girl took all the bridal garments and ornaments prepared for marriage and burned them, then threw herself into the fire; her parents rescued and stopped her.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhao died suddenly. The girl gathered every garment and ornament prepared for her wedding and burned them, then threw herself into the flames. Her parents pulled her back.

sentences.zh: 乃赴翁家，哀告舅姑乞立嗣，復乞一小樓，設夫位，坐臥於旁，奠食相對，非姑不接面。

translations.literal: She then went to the Weng household, tearfully begged her parents-in-law to establish an heir, and further begged for a small upper chamber, set up her husband's spirit seat, sat and slept beside it, offered food facing it, and would not show her face except to her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She went to her betrothed's home, pleaded with his parents to name an heir, and asked for a small chamber where she set up her husband's spirit tablet. There she lived, eating before his tablet, and would show her face to no one but her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 舅亡，家落，忍饑紡績以養姑。

translations.literal: When her father-in-law died, the family declined; she endured hunger and spun and wove to support her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: After her father-in-law died the family fell on hard times. She went hungry herself while spinning and weaving to feed her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 未幾，姑亦亡，鄰火大起，夜半達旦，延百餘家。

translations.literal: Before long her mother-in-law also died; a neighbor's fire broke out on a grand scale—from midnight until dawn it spread to more than a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon her mother-in-law died too. A fire broke out next door and raged from midnight until dawn, spreading to more than a hundred homes.

sentences.zh: 鄰婦趨上樓，勸之避，婦曰：「此正我授命時也。」

translations.literal: A neighbor woman rushed upstairs and urged her to flee; the wife said: "This is precisely the time for me to surrender my life."
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor rushed upstairs to urge her to flee. The widow said, "This is my moment to surrender my life."

sentences.zh: 抱夫木主待焚。

translations.literal: She embraced her husband's spirit tablet and awaited the burning.
translations.idiomatic: She clasped her husband's spirit tablet and waited for the flames.

sentences.zh: 須臾四面皆燼，小樓獨存。

translations.literal: In a moment everything on all sides was ashes; the small chamber alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Within moments everything around her was reduced to ashes—but the small chamber stood untouched.

sentences.zh: 玉亭縣君，伊府宗室典柄女。

translations.literal: The Lady of Yuting County was the daughter of Dian Bing of the Yi Prince's line of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Yuting County was the daughter of Dian Bing, of the Yi Prince's line in the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，適楊仞。

translations.literal: At age twenty-four she married Yang Ren.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four she married Yang Ren.

sentences.zh: 不兩月仞卒，號慟不食。

translations.literal: In less than two months Ren died; she wailed in grief and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Less than two months later Yang Ren died. She wailed in grief and refused all food.

sentences.zh: 或勸以舅姑年老，且有遺孕，乃忍死襄事。

translations.literal: Some urged her that her parents-in-law were old and she was pregnant with her late husband's child; she then steeled herself to live and manage the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When others reminded her that his parents were elderly and she was carrying his child, she forced herself to live and see the funeral through.

sentences.zh: 及生男，家日落。

translations.literal: When she gave birth to a son, the family's fortunes declined day by day.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son, but the family's fortunes only worsened.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十一年，河南大饑，宗祿久缺，紡績三日，不得一飧，母子相持慟哭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Wanli, a great famine struck Henan; the clan stipend had long gone unpaid; after three days of spinning and weaving they could not get one meal; mother and son clung to each other and wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Wanli a great famine struck Henan. The clan stipend had long gone unpaid. After three days of spinning they had not a single meal. Mother and son clung to each other, weeping.

sentences.zh: 夜分夢神語曰：「汝節行上聞於天，當有以相助。」

translations.literal: In the deep of night she dreamed a spirit spoke, saying: "Your chaste conduct has reached heaven above; you shall receive aid."
translations.idiomatic: Deep in the night she dreamed a voice saying, "Your steadfast fidelity has reached heaven—you will be helped."

sentences.zh: 晨興，母子述所夢皆符，頗怪之。

translations.literal: At dawn when they rose, mother and son described their dreams and found they matched; they thought it quite strange.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn mother and son compared their dreams and found they matched perfectly. They marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 其子曰：「取屋后土作坯，易粟。」

translations.literal: Her son said: "Take earth from behind the house, make clay blocks, and exchange them for grain."
translations.idiomatic: Her son said, "Let us dig earth behind the house, make clay bricks, and trade them for grain."

sentences.zh: 其日掘土，得錢數百。

translations.literal: That day when they dug earth, they obtained several hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: That day they dug—and found several hundred coins.

sentences.zh: 自是，每掘輒得錢。

translations.literal: From then on, every time they dug they obtained money.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every time they dug they found money.

sentences.zh: 一日，舍傍地陷，得石炭一窖，取以供爨。

translations.literal: One day the ground beside the house collapsed, and they obtained a vault of coal; they took it to supply their cooking hearth.
translations.idiomatic: One day the ground beside the house collapsed, revealing a cache of coal they used for cooking.

sentences.zh: 延兩月餘，官俸亦至，人以為苦節所感。

translations.literal: This lasted for more than two months; the official salary also arrived; people thought it was moved by her steadfast chastity through hardship.
translations.idiomatic: For two more months they lived on this bounty; then the official stipend finally arrived. People took it as a reward for her steadfast fidelity.

sentences.zh: 馬節婦，年十六，歸平湖諸生劉濂。

translations.literal: Chaste Widow Ma, aged sixteen, married the licentiate Liu Lian of Pinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Widow Ma was sixteen when she married Liu Lian, a licentiate of Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 十七而寡。

translations.literal: At seventeen she became a widow.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen she was widowed.

sentences.zh: 翁家甚貧，利其再適，必欲奪其志。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law's family was very poor; seeing profit in her remarriage, they were determined to overcome her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's family was desperately poor and saw profit in forcing her to remarry—they would stop at nothing to break her resolve.

sentences.zh: 不與飲食，百計挫之，誌益厲。

translations.literal: They gave her no food or drink; they tried a hundred schemes to break her down, but her resolve grew only fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: They denied her food and drink and tried every scheme to break her—but her resolve only hardened.

sentences.zh: 嘗閉門自經，或救之，則系絕而墜於地死矣。

translations.literal: Once she closed the door to hang herself; when someone tried to rescue her, the rope broke and she fell to the ground, as if dead.
translations.idiomatic: Once she shut her door to hang herself. When rescuers rushed in, the rope snapped and she crashed to the floor, apparently lifeless.

sentences.zh: 急解之，漸蘇。

translations.literal: They hurriedly freed her, and gradually she revived.
translations.idiomatic: They rushed to free her, and after a time she came back to consciousness.

sentences.zh: 翁又陰納沈氏聘，其姑誘與俱出，令女奴抱持納沈舟。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law again secretly accepted betrothal from the Shen clan; her mother-in-law lured her to go out together and had maidservants seize and carry her into Shen's boat.
translations.idiomatic: Her father-in-law secretly accepted a betrothal from the Shen family. Her mother-in-law coaxed her out on an errand, and maidservants seized her and put her aboard Shen's boat.

sentences.zh: 婦投河不得，疾呼天救我。

translations.literal: The wife tried to throw herself in the river but could not; she cried urgently, "Heaven, save me!"
translations.idiomatic: She tried to throw herself into the river but could not. Desperately she cried, "Heaven, save me!"

sentences.zh: 須臾風雨晝晦，疾雷擊舟，欲覆者數四。

translations.literal: In a moment wind and rain made the day dark; fierce thunder struck the boat, which nearly capsized four times.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly wind and rain blotted out the daylight. Thunder struck the boat again and again; four times it nearly capsized.

sentences.zh: 沈懼，乃旋舟還之。

translations.literal: Shen was frightened and turned the boat and returned her.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shen turned the boat around and sent her back.

sentences.zh: 事聞於縣，縣令婦別居。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the county, the magistrate had the wife live separately.
translations.idiomatic: When the county magistrate learned of the affair, he ordered the widow to live apart from her in-laws.

sentences.zh: 時父兄盡歿，無可歸，假寓一學舍，官贍之以老。

translations.literal: At that time her father and brothers had all died; she had nowhere to return; she lodged temporarily in a schoolhouse; the government supported her until old age.
translations.idiomatic: By then her father and brothers were all dead and she had nowhere to go. The magistrate lodged her in a schoolhouse and provided for her until the end of her days.

sentences.zh: 王氏，東莞葉其瑞妻。

translations.literal: Lady Wang was the wife of Ye Qirui of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was the wife of Ye Qirui of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 其瑞貧，操舟往來鄰境，一月一歸。

translations.literal: Qirui was poor; he plied a boat back and forth to neighboring districts, returning once a month.
translations.idiomatic: Qirui was poor and made his living ferrying goods to neighboring districts, returning home once a month.

sentences.zh: 婦紡績易食。

translations.literal: The wife spun and wove to exchange for food.
translations.idiomatic: His wife spun and wove thread to barter for food.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十四年，嶺南大饑，民多鬻妻子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Wanli, a great famine struck Lingnan; many people sold their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Wanli a great famine struck Lingnan, and many sold their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 其瑞將鬻婦博羅民家，券成，載其人俱來。

translations.literal: Qirui was about to sell his wife to a commoner family in Boluo; the contract was completed, and he brought that person with him together.
translations.idiomatic: Qirui arranged to sell his wife to a Boluo buyer. The contract was signed, and he brought the buyer home with him.

sentences.zh: 入門見氏羸甚，問之，不饘粥數日矣。

translations.literal: Entering the door he saw the lady was extremely wasted; asking her, she had had no gruel for several days.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered, the buyer found the wife terribly emaciated—she had not eaten even gruel for days.

sentences.zh: 其瑞泣語之故，且示之金，婦笑而許之。

translations.literal: Qirui tearfully told the reason, and also showed her the money; the wife smiled and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Qirui tearfully explained why he had come and showed her the money. She smiled and agreed.

sentences.zh: 及舟發寶潭，躍入潭中死。

translations.literal: When the boat set out from Baotan, she leaped into the pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the boat put out from Baotan, she leaped into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 兩岸觀者如堵，皆謂水迅，屍流無所底。

translations.literal: Spectators on both banks were thick as a wall; all said the current was swift and the corpse would drift with nowhere to come to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds lined both banks. Everyone said the current was too swift for her body ever to be found.

sentences.zh: 其瑞至，從上流哭數聲，屍忽湧出，去所投處，已逆流數十步矣。

translations.literal: When Qirui arrived, he wailed several cries upstream; the corpse suddenly surged forth, already dozens of paces upstream from where she had thrown herself against the current.
translations.idiomatic: When Qirui arrived and wept upstream, her body suddenly rose to the surface—already dozens of paces upstream from where she had entered the water, against the current.

sentences.zh: 劉氏，博平吳進學妻。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was the wife of Wu Jinxiang of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu was the wife of Wu Jinxiang of Boping.

sentences.zh: 楊氏，進性妻。

translations.literal: Lady Yang was the wife of Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was the wife of Wu Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 進學疫死，既葬，劉夜匍匐縊於墓所。

translations.literal: Jinxiang died of pestilence; once buried, Liu crawled at night and hanged herself at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxiang died in an epidemic. After the burial, Liu crawled to the grave at night and hanged herself beside it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進性亦疫死，楊一慟幾絕。

translations.literal: Before long Jinxing also died of pestilence; Yang wailed once in grief and nearly expired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jinxing died of the same plague. Yang was so stricken with grief she nearly expired.

sentences.zh: 姑議嫁之，楊曰：「我何以不如姒。」

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law discussed remarrying her; Yang said: "Why am I any less than my sister-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law proposed remarriage, Yang said, "Why should I fall short of my sister-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 遂縊死。

translations.literal: Then she hanged herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself at once.

sentences.zh: 譚氏，南海方存業妻。

translations.literal: Lady Tan was the wife of Fang Cunye of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tan was the wife of Fang Cunye of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 生子三月，夫亡，悲號欲殉。

translations.literal: Three months after bearing a son, her husband died; she wailed in grief and wished to follow him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Three months after her son was born, her husband died. She wailed and wished to die with him.

sentences.zh: 母乃姑交止之，且諷改適。

translations.literal: Her mother and mother-in-law together stopped her, and also subtly urged her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother and mother-in-law together held her back, gently suggesting she might remarry.

sentences.zh: 氏垂涕曰：「吾久不樂生，特念姑與兒耳。」

translations.literal: Tan said with tears streaming: "I have long not rejoiced in life; I only think of my mother-in-law and my child."
translations.idiomatic: Through her tears she said, "I have long ceased to wish for life—I endure only for my mother-in-law and my son."

sentences.zh: 哽咽流涕不止，二人不敢復言。

translations.literal: She choked with sobs and tears flowed without cease; the two did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: She sobbed until neither dared press her again.

sentences.zh: 及子七歲，遣就塾師，先令拜姑，微示付托意，竊自喜曰：「吾今可以遂誌矣。」

translations.literal: When her son was seven, she sent him to a school tutor; first she had him bow to his grandmother, subtly showing her intent of entrustment; she said secretly to herself with satisfaction: "Now I can fulfill my wish."
translations.idiomatic: When her son turned seven she sent him to school. First she had him bow to his grandmother, hinting that she entrusted the boy to her care. Secretly she rejoiced: "At last I may fulfill my resolve."

sentences.zh: 一日，媒氏至，復勸改適，氏愈憤，中夜縊死。

translations.literal: One day a matchmaker came and again urged remarriage; Tan grew all the more indignant; in the middle of the night she hanged herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: One day a matchmaker came urging remarriage again. Tan's indignation only deepened—and in the depth of night she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 又張氏，臨清林與岐妻。

translations.literal: Also Lady Zhang, wife of Lin Yuqi of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Zhang, wife of Lin Yuqi of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 夫亡，欲自縊，舅姑慰之曰：「爾死，如遺孤何？」

translations.literal: When her husband died, she wished to hang herself; her parents-in-law comforted her, saying: "If you die, what of the orphan left behind?"
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died she prepared to hang herself. Her in-laws pleaded, "If you die, what becomes of your orphaned child?"

sentences.zh: 氏以衣物倩乳嫗育其子，三月，知子安乳嫗，遂不食死。

translations.literal: Zhang entrusted her clothing to a wet nurse to raise her son; after three months, knowing her son was settled with the wet nurse, she then stopped eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: She left her child's garments with a wet nurse to raise the boy. After three months, satisfied that he was thriving, she stopped eating and died.

sentences.zh: 李烈婦，餘姚吳江妻。

translations.literal: Chaste Wife Li was the wife of Wu Jiang of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Wife Li was the wife of Wu Jiang of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 年二十，夫與舅俱卒，家酷貧，婦紡績養姑，己恒凍餒。

translations.literal: Aged twenty, her husband and father-in-law both died; the family was desperately poor; the wife spun and wove to support her mother-in-law, while she herself was always cold and hungry.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty, her husband and father-in-law died in succession. The family was desperately poor. She spun and wove to feed her mother-in-law while she herself went cold and hungry.

sentences.zh: 有黃某者，謀娶之，賄夫族某使鉺其姑，未即從。

translations.literal: A certain Huang plotted to marry her; he bribed a certain member of her husband's clan to entice her mother-in-law, but she did not immediately consent.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Huang sought to marry her. He bribed a clansman to win over her mother-in-law, but she would not yield at once.

sentences.zh: 某乃陰與黃及父家約，詭稱其母暴病，肩輿來迎。

translations.literal: That person then secretly arranged with Huang and her father's family, falsely claiming her mother had suddenly fallen ill, and a sedan chair came to fetch her.
translations.idiomatic: The clansman then secretly conspired with Huang and her father's family. They falsely claimed her mother had taken suddenly ill and sent a sedan chair to fetch her.

sentences.zh: 婦倉卒升輿，既及門，非父家也。

translations.literal: The wife in haste entered the sedan; when she reached the gate, it was not her father's home.
translations.idiomatic: The widow entered the chair in haste—but when it stopped, she found herself not at her father's house.

sentences.zh: 姑亦尋至，布幾席，速使成禮。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law also soon arrived; they spread tables and mats and hurried to complete the marriage ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law arrived shortly after. They spread mats and rushed the wedding ceremony.

sentences.zh: 婦佯曰：「所以不欲嫁者，為姑老無依耳。

translations.literal: The wife feigned, saying: "The reason I did not wish to marry was only that my mother-in-law was old with no one to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: The widow feigned acquiescence: "The only reason I resisted remarriage was that my mother-in-law is old and has no one to rely on.

sentences.zh: 姑既許，復何言。

translations.literal: Now that my mother-in-law has agreed, what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: Now that she has consented, what objection can I raise?

sentences.zh: 然妾自夫歿未嘗解帶，今願一洗沐。」

translations.literal: Yet since my husband's death I have never unfastened my sash; now I wish to wash once."
translations.idiomatic: But since my husband died I have never unbound my sash. Allow me first to bathe."

sentences.zh: 又問：「聘財幾何？」

translations.literal: She also asked: "How much was the betrothal wealth?"
translations.idiomatic: She also asked, "How much was the bride-price?"

sentences.zh: 姑以數對。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law answered with the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law named the sum.

sentences.zh: 曰：「亟懷之去。

translations.literal: She said: "Quickly take it and go.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Take it away with you at once.

sentences.zh: 姑在，我即從人，殊赧顏也。」

translations.literal: With my mother-in-law present, if I follow another man at once, how utterly shameful my face would be."
translations.idiomatic: With my mother-in-law watching, I would be too ashamed to go to another man's bed."

sentences.zh: 眾喜，促姑行，為具湯。

translations.literal: Everyone rejoiced; they urged the mother-in-law to leave and prepared bathwater.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, they urged the mother-in-law to leave and prepared bathwater.

sentences.zh: 湯至，久不出，辟戶視之，則縊死矣。

translations.literal: When the water came, she did not emerge for a long time; opening the door to look, they found she had hanged herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: The water was ready, but she did not emerge. When they forced the door, she was hanging dead.

sentences.zh: 其後，崇禎十五年，餘姚又有黃烈婦者，金一龍妻。

translations.literal: Later, in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, in Yuyao there was again Chaste Wife Huang, wife of Jin Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, Yuyao produced another Chaste Wife Huang, wife of Jin Yilong.

sentences.zh: 夫早歿，黃截指自誓，立從子為嗣，與姑相依。

translations.literal: Her husband died early; Huang cut her finger to swear herself, established a nephew as heir, and lived in mutual dependence with her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband died young. Huang cut off a finger to bind her vow, named a nephew as heir, and lived with her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 熊氏子欲娶之，母黨利其財，紿令還家，間道送於熊。

translations.literal: The son of the Xiong clan wished to marry her; her mother's relatives coveted her property; they deceived her into returning home and sent her by a side path to the Xiong household.
translations.idiomatic: A Xiong family son sought to marry her. Her mother's relatives, coveting her property, lured her home and smuggled her by a back road to the Xiong household.

sentences.zh: 黃知勢不可挽，願搜括所有以償聘金，不聽，相持至夜深，引刀自刎未殞。

translations.literal: Huang knew the situation could not be reversed; she wished to gather all her possessions to repay the betrothal gold; they did not listen; they struggled until deep into the night; she drew a knife and cut her throat but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Huang saw she could not resist. She offered everything she owned to repay the bride-price, but they refused. The struggle lasted deep into the night until she drew a knife and cut her throat—but did not die.

sentences.zh: 其姑聞之，急趨視，黃曰：「婦所以未即死者，欲姑一面耳，今復何求。」

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law heard and hurried to look; Huang said: "The reason your daughter-in-law has not died at once is that she wished to see her mother-in-law once more; now what more is there to seek?"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law rushed in. Huang said, "I have lived only to see you one last time. Now I want nothing more."

sentences.zh: 遂剜喉以絕。

translations.literal: Then she gouged her throat to end her life.
translations.idiomatic: She gouged open her throat and died.

sentences.zh: 郡邑聞之，斃熊氏子獄中。

translations.literal: When the prefecture and county learned of it, they beat the Xiong clan's son to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities learned of the affair, the Xiong son died under beatings in prison.

sentences.zh: 須烈婦，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Chaste Wife Xu was from Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Wife Xu was from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 夫李死，市兒悅其色，爭欲娶之。

translations.literal: When her husband Li died, market youths admired her beauty and vied to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband Li died, market youths who admired her beauty competed to marry her.

sentences.zh: 婦泣曰：「吾方送一夫，旋迎一夫。

translations.literal: The wife wept, saying: "I have just sent off one husband—am I now to welcome another?
translations.idiomatic: She wept, "I have just buried one husband—must I take another so soon?

sentences.zh: 且利吾夫之死而妻我，不猶殺我夫耶！」

translations.literal: Moreover, to profit from my husband's death and make me their wife—is that not the same as killing my husband!"
translations.idiomatic: And to profit from my husband's death by making me a wife—is that not as good as murdering him yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 市兒乃糾黨聚謀，將掠之。

translations.literal: The market youths then gathered a gang to plot together, intending to abduct her.
translations.idiomatic: The youths banded together and plotted to abduct her by force.

sentences.zh: 婦驚奔母，母懼不敢留。

translations.literal: The wife fled in alarm to her mother; her mother was afraid and dared not keep her.
translations.idiomatic: She fled in terror to her mother's house. Her mother, afraid, would not shelter her.

sentences.zh: 返於姑，姑懼知母。

translations.literal: She returned to her mother-in-law; her mother-in-law was afraid, knowing her mother had not kept her.
translations.idiomatic: She turned back to her mother-in-law—but her mother-in-law, too, was afraid to shelter her, knowing her own mother had refused.

sentences.zh: 投姊，姊益不敢留，婦泣而歸。

translations.literal: She went to her elder sister; her sister, even more, dared not keep her. The wife wept and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: She sought refuge with her elder sister, but her sister, too, was afraid to take her in. Weeping, the wife returned home.

sentences.zh: 鄰人勸之曰：「若即死，誰旌若節者，何自苦若此？」

translations.literal: A neighbor urged her, saying: "If you die at once, who will commend your chastity? Why torment yourself like this?"
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor tried to persuade her: "If you die now, who will proclaim your virtue to the world? Why torment yourself like this?"

sentences.zh: 婦度終不免，自經死。

translations.literal: The wife judged that she could not ultimately escape, and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Concluding that there was no escape, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 陳節婦，安陸人。

translations.literal: Chaste Wife Chen was from Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste Wife Chen was a native of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 適李姓，早寡，孑然一身，歸父家守志，坐臥小樓，足不下樓者三十年。

translations.literal: She married into the Li family, was widowed early, and alone returned to her father's house to keep her vows. For thirty years she sat and slept in a small tower, her feet never leaving the stairs.
translations.idiomatic: She had married a man of the Li clan and was widowed young. Alone, she returned to her father's house to uphold her widowhood. For thirty years she lived on a small upper floor, never once setting foot off the staircase.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂其婢曰：「吾死，慎勿以男子舁我。」

translations.literal: On her deathbed she told her maid: "When I die, take care not to let any man carry me."
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she told her maid: "When I die, see that no man carries my body."

sentences.zh: 家人忽其言，令男子登樓舉之，氣絕逾時矣，起坐曰：「始我何言，而令若輩至此。」

translations.literal: The family disregarded her words and had men go upstairs to lift her. Her breath had already ceased for some time when she sat up and said: "What did I say at the start, that you have brought yourselves to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The family disregarded her warning and sent men upstairs to carry her down. Her breath had already stopped for some time when she sat up and said: "What did I tell you, that you have brought yourselves to this?"

sentences.zh: 家人驚怖而下，目乃瞑。

translations.literal: The family, startled and terrified, went down. Only then did her eyes close.
translations.idiomatic: The family, stricken with terror, withdrew. Only then did her eyes close.

sentences.zh: 馬氏，山陰劉晉嘯妻。

translations.literal: Lady Ma was the wife of Liu Jinxiao of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ma was the wife of Liu Jinxiao of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，晉嘯客死，馬年二十許，家無立錐。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign, Jinxiao died away from home. Ma was about twenty, and the household had not so much as standing room for an awl.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Jinxiao died far from home. Ma was about twenty, and the family was so destitute they lacked even standing room for an awl.

sentences.zh: 伯氏有樓，遂與母寄居其上，以十指給養，不下梯者數十年。

translations.literal: Her husband's elder brother had a tower; she and her mother took lodgings there, supporting themselves by the work of her ten fingers. For decades she did not descend the ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's elder brother owned a tower, and she and her mother took refuge there. She supported them both by the labor of her own hands. For decades she never once came down the ladder.

sentences.zh: 常用瓦盆貯新土，以足附之。

translations.literal: She often kept fresh earth in a pottery bowl and pressed her feet against it.
translations.idiomatic: She kept a pottery bowl filled with fresh earth and pressed her feet against it.

sentences.zh: 鄰婦問故，曰：「吾以服土氣耳。」

translations.literal: A neighboring woman asked why; she said: "I do this to absorb the earth's vital energy."
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor asked why, she said: "I do this to draw nourishment from the earth's vital energy."

sentences.zh: 年六十五卒。

translations.literal: She died at the age of sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 謝烈婦，名玉華，番禺曹世興妻。

translations.literal: Virtuous Wife Xie, named Yuhua, was the wife of Cao Shixing of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Wife Xie, whose given name was Yuhua, was the wife of Cao Shixing of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 世興為馮氏塾師，甫成婚，即負笈往。

translations.literal: Shixing was a tutor for the Feng clan. As soon as the marriage was concluded, he set off with his book bundle.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing served as a tutor to the Feng clan. No sooner was the marriage concluded than he set off with his book bundle.

sentences.zh: 亡何病歸，不能起，婦誓不改適。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home ill, unable to rise. The wife vowed never to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned home gravely ill and could not rise from his bed. His wife vowed never to remarry.

sentences.zh: 曹族之老嘉之，議分祭田以贍。

translations.literal: The elders of the Cao clan praised this and proposed dividing sacrificial estate lands to support her.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of the Cao clan praised her resolve and proposed dividing sacrificial estate lands to provide for her.

sentences.zh: 或謂婦年方盛，當俟襄事畢，令歸寧，婦佯諾。

translations.literal: Some said the wife was still in the prime of life and ought, once the funeral rites were complete, to be sent back to her parents for a visit. The wife feigned consent.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that she was still young and ought, once the funeral rites were complete, to be sent home to her parents for a visit. The wife pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 及期，駕輿欲行，別諸姒，多作訣語，徐入室閉戶，以刀自斷其頸。

translations.literal: When the day came, a carriage was harnessed for her departure. She took leave of her sisters-in-law with many words of farewell, then slowly entered a room, shut the door, and cut her own neck with a knife.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, a carriage was readied for her departure. She bade farewell to her sisters-in-law with many parting words, then slowly entered a room, shut the door, and severed her own neck with a knife.

sentences.zh: 家人亟穴板入，血流滿衣，尚未絕，見諸人入，亟以左手從斷處探喉出之，右手引刀一割，乃瞑。

translations.literal: The family hurriedly bored through the door panel to enter. Blood soaked her clothes; she was not yet dead. Seeing them come in, she quickly reached with her left hand from the wound into her throat and pulled it out, then with her right hand drew the knife and cut once more—only then did her eyes close.
translations.idiomatic: The family hurriedly bored through the door panel to reach her. Blood soaked her clothes, yet she had not died. Seeing them enter, she quickly reached with her left hand into the wound and pulled her throat free, then with her right hand drew the knife and cut again—only then did her eyes close.

sentences.zh: 張氏，桐城李棟妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang was the wife of Li Dong of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang was the wife of Li Dong of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 棟死無子，張自經於床。

translations.literal: Dong died without sons. Zhang hanged herself on the bed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong died without an heir, Zhang hanged herself on the bed.

sentences.zh: 母救之，奮身起，引斧斫左臂者三。

translations.literal: Her mother rescued her. She sprang up, seized an axe, and struck her left arm three times.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother cut her down. She sprang up, seized an axe, and hacked at her left arm three times.

sentences.zh: 家人奪斧，抑而坐之蓐間，張瞆悶不語。

translations.literal: The family snatched away the axe, forced her to sit on the matting, and Zhang sat dazed and silent.
translations.idiomatic: The family wrested away the axe and forced her to sit on the matting. Zhang sat dazed and would not speak.

sentences.zh: 家人稍退，張遽揜身出戶投於水。

translations.literal: When the family withdrew a little, Zhang suddenly slipped out and threw herself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: When the family withdrew a little, Zhang suddenly slipped out of the house and threw herself into the water.

sentences.zh: 水方冰，以首觸穴入，遂死。」

translations.literal: The water was just freezing over. She broke through the ice with her head and entered; thus she died."
translations.idiomatic: The water had just begun to freeze. She broke through the ice with her head and sank beneath it, and so died."

sentences.zh: 邑又有烈婦王氏，高文學妻。

translations.literal: In the district there was also the virtuous widow Lady Wang, wife of Gao Wenxue.
translations.idiomatic: In the same district there was also the virtuous widow Lady Wang, wife of Gao Wenxue.

sentences.zh: 文學死，父道美來吊，謂王曰：「無過哀。

translations.literal: When Wenxue died, his father Daomei came to offer condolences and said to Wang: "Do not grieve excessively.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxue died, his father Daomei came to offer condolences and said to Wang: "Do not grieve beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 事有三等，在汝自為之。」

translations.literal: There are three courses of action—the choice is yours."
translations.idiomatic: There are three courses of action. The choice is yours."

sentences.zh: 王輟泣問之，父曰：「其一從夫地下為烈，次則冰霜以事翁姑為節，三則恒人事也。」

translations.literal: Wang stopped weeping and asked what he meant. The father said: "The first is to follow your husband underground—that is martyrdom. Next is to serve your parents-in-law with frost-like steadfastness—that is chastity. The third is ordinary human conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Wang stopped weeping and asked what he meant. The father said: "The first is to follow your husband into the grave—that is martyrdom. The second is to serve your parents-in-law with frost-like steadfastness—that is chastity. The third is the ordinary course of life."

sentences.zh: 王即鍵戶，絕粒不食，越七日而死。

translations.literal: Wang immediately barred the door, ceased eating altogether, and after seven days she died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang immediately barred the door, stopped eating altogether, and died seven days later.

sentences.zh: 又有戚家婦者，寶應人。

translations.literal: There was also a woman of the Qi family, from Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a woman of the Qi family, from Baoying.

sentences.zh: 甫合巹，而夫暴歿。

translations.literal: She had just joined in the wedding cup when her husband suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: She had just shared the wedding cup when her husband suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 婦哭之哀，投門外汪中死。

translations.literal: The wife wailed in deep grief and threw herself into the pond outside the gate to die.
translations.idiomatic: The wife wailed in deep grief and threw herself into the pond outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 後人名其死所為戚家汪云。

translations.literal: Later generations named the place of her death Qi Family Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations named the place of her death Qi Family Pond.

sentences.zh: 金氏，通渭劉大俊妻。

translations.literal: Lady Jin was the wife of Liu Dajun of Tongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jin was the wife of Liu Dajun of Tongwei.

sentences.zh: 年十九，夫病風痹，金扶浴溫泉。

translations.literal: At nineteen, her husband suffered from wind paralysis. Jin supported him to bathe in hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, her husband was stricken with paralytic illness. Jin supported him as he bathed in hot springs.

sentences.zh: 暴風雨，山水陡發，夫不能動，令金急走。

translations.literal: A sudden violent storm; the mountain waters burst forth. Her husband could not move and told Jin to flee at once.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden violent storm sent mountain torrents rushing down. Her husband could not move and urged Jin to flee at once.

sentences.zh: 金號泣堅持不肯舍，並溺死。

translations.literal: Jin wailed and steadfastly refused to let go; both drowned together.
translations.idiomatic: Jin wept and clung to him, refusing to let go, and both drowned together.

sentences.zh: 屍流數十里而出，手猶挽夫不釋云。

translations.literal: Their corpses were carried downstream for several tens of li before emerging; her hand still clutched her husband and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Their bodies were carried downstream for many li before surfacing; her hand still clutched her husband and would not let go.

sentences.zh: 又應山諸生王芳妻楊氏。

translations.literal: Also Lady Yang, wife of Wang Fang, a licentiate of Yingshan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Yang, wife of Wang Fang, a licentiate of Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 芳醉墜塘中，氏赴水救之。

translations.literal: Fang, drunk, fell into a pond. Yang rushed into the water to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, drunk, fell into a pond. Yang plunged into the water to save him.

sentences.zh: 夫入水益深，氏追深處偕死。

translations.literal: Her husband sank deeper into the water. Yang pursued him into the depths and died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband sank deeper into the water. Yang followed him into the depths and died with him.

sentences.zh: 王氏，山陰沈伯燮妻。

translations.literal: Lady Wang was the wife of Shen Boyie of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was the wife of Shen Boyie of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 議婚數年，伯燮病厲，手攣發禿，父母有他意。

translations.literal: Their marriage had been under negotiation for years when Boyie fell gravely ill—his hands crippled, his hair fallen out. His parents began to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: Their marriage had been under negotiation for years when Boyie fell gravely ill, his hands crippled and his hair fallen out. His parents began to reconsider the match.

sentences.zh: 女問：「沈郎病始何日？」

translations.literal: The girl asked: "When did Master Shen's illness begin?"
translations.idiomatic: The girl asked: "When did Master Shen's illness begin?"

sentences.zh: 父曰：「初許時固佳兒，今乃病。」

translations.literal: Her father said: "When we first pledged you, he was indeed a fine young man. Now he is ill."
translations.idiomatic: Her father said: "When we first pledged you to him, he was a fine young man. Now he is ill."

sentences.zh: 女曰：「既許而病，命也，違命不祥。」

translations.literal: She said: "The pledge was made, and then he fell ill—that is fate. To break a pledged match is ill-omened."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "The pledge was made, and then he fell ill—that is fate. To break a pledged match is ill-omened."

sentences.zh: 竟歸之。

translations.literal: She went through with the marriage after all.
translations.idiomatic: She went through with the marriage after all.

sentences.zh: 伯燮病且憊，王奉事無少怠。

translations.literal: Boyie was grievously ill and failing; Wang served him without the slightest slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Boyie was gravely ill and failing fast. Wang tended him without the slightest slackening.

sentences.zh: 居八年卒，嗣其從子。

translations.literal: After eight years of marriage he died. She adopted his younger cousin as heir.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years of marriage he died. She adopted his younger cousin as heir.

sentences.zh: 更出簪珥佐舅買妾，更得子。

translations.literal: She further sold hairpins and earrings to help her father-in-law buy a concubine, and thus a son was born.
